_comment: Source of truth for statements. A statement with "status": "candidate" is answered by audits but not asked in the test until it carries signal on the real dividing lines (test 2, audits/statements/STANDARD.md); an active statement that loses it is demoted back to candidate. Adding or removing a statement leaves existing audits valid; rewording one needs a new id. The agree/disagree/note/icon fields explain each statement to test takers and do not affect audits.

statements.text: The government should provide universal healthcare.
statements.agree: Everyone gets health care paid for or guaranteed by the state, usually through taxes.
statements.disagree: The government should not provide universal healthcare.
statements.note: About the state guaranteeing health care for everyone, whether it runs the services or pays for them. Public care only for the poor is not enough.

statements.text: The legal minimum wage should cover a full-time worker's basic living costs.
statements.agree: Full-time work at the legal wage floor should pay enough to meet basic living costs.
statements.disagree: The legal minimum wage need not cover a full-time worker's basic living costs.
statements.note: About the level of the legal wage floor: whether full-time work at it should cover basic costs such as rent and food. Having a minimum wage at all is a different question.

statements.text: Free markets allocate resources better than governments do.
statements.agree: Prices and competition generally decide better than officials what gets made and who gets it.
statements.disagree: Free markets do not allocate resources better than governments do.
statements.note: About which generally decides better what gets made and who gets it: prices and competition, or officials. Accepting some regulation or public services doesn't count against it.

statements.text: Major industries should be publicly owned.
statements.agree: Industries such as energy, rail and utilities should be owned by the state or public bodies, not private companies.
statements.disagree: Major industries should not be publicly owned.
statements.note: About state or public ownership of key industries such as energy, rail and utilities. Regulating private firms, or owning a single company, is not the same.

statements.text: The wealthy should pay a much larger share of their income in tax than others.
statements.agree: High earners and the very rich should pay tax at a much higher rate than everyone else.
statements.disagree: The wealthy should not pay a much larger share of their income in tax than others.
statements.note: About tax rates: whether the rich should pay a much higher share of their income than others, not just more money in total.

statements.text: Labor unions benefit workers.
statements.agree: Workers benefit from labor unions.
statements.disagree: Workers do not benefit from labor unions.
statements.note: About unions' effects on workers generally. This does not endorse every union leader, compulsory membership, every strike, or a particular relationship with the state.

statements.text: Private property is a fundamental right that should be very hard to override.
statements.agree: Owners' rights to their property should almost never be overridden, even for public goals.
statements.disagree: Private property is not a fundamental right that should be very hard to override.
statements.note: About how far the state may limit or take private property, for example to build roads, control rents or plan land use.

statements.text: Corporations should face strict government regulation.
statements.agree: Government should impose strict rules on how corporations operate.
statements.disagree: Corporations should not face strict government regulation.
statements.note: About strict rules on how companies operate, for example on safety, pollution or competition. Basic rules such as contract law are not enough.

statements.text: Workers should collectively own the businesses they work in.
statements.agree: Businesses should belong to the people who work in them, for example as cooperatives.
statements.disagree: Workers should not collectively own the businesses they work in.
statements.note: About workers owning their firms together, as in cooperatives. Employee share schemes or state ownership are not the same.

statements.text: Government surveillance to prevent terrorism is acceptable.
statements.agree: It is acceptable for the government to monitor people when that helps prevent terrorism.
statements.disagree: Government surveillance is not acceptable, even to prevent terrorism.
statements.note: About the government monitoring communications or movements to prevent terrorism. Caring about security, or about civil liberties, is not the same as taking a side on this.

statements.text: Recreational drugs should be legal for adults.
statements.agree: Adults may legally buy and use drugs such as cannabis, possibly with regulation.
statements.disagree: Recreational drugs should be illegal for adults.
statements.note: About legal sale and use of recreational drugs by adults, not only decriminalising possession or allowing medical use.

statements.text: Hate speech should be legally restricted.
statements.agree: Speech that attacks groups for who they are can be punished by law.
statements.disagree: Hate speech should be legal.
statements.note: About making speech that attacks people for who they are a legal offence. Social disapproval, or bans on direct threats, are not the same.

statements.text: A strong leader able to bypass political gridlock would benefit the country.
statements.agree: The country would benefit from a strong leader with the power to act despite deadlock among its political institutions.
statements.disagree: A strong leader able to bypass political gridlock would not benefit the country.
statements.note: About giving one leader the power to act when parliament and parties are stuck.

statements.text: The state should be abolished.
statements.agree: Society would be better off without governments at all.
statements.disagree: The state should not be abolished.
statements.note: About doing away with government entirely. Wanting a much smaller state is a different position.

statements.text: Gun ownership should be strictly limited.
statements.agree: Gun ownership should be strictly limited by law.
statements.disagree: Gun ownership should not be strictly limited.
statements.note: About strict limits on who may own guns and which guns, not only background checks or other light rules.

statements.text: Sex work between consenting adults should be legal.
statements.agree: Adults can legally sell sexual services to other consenting adults.
statements.disagree: Sex work between consenting adults should be illegal.
statements.note: About whether selling sex between consenting adults should be legal. Laws against trafficking or coercion are a different question.

statements.text: Decisions should be made as locally as possible.
statements.agree: Political decisions should rest with the smallest local community able to handle them, with wider authorities handling matters that need a wider reach.
statements.disagree: Decisions should not be made as locally as possible.
statements.note: About where decisions sit by default: with the smallest community able to handle them. Having some local government is not enough.

statements.text: Prisons should focus more on rehabilitation than on punishment.
statements.agree: Prisons should mainly help offenders rejoin society.
statements.disagree: Prisons should focus at least as much on punishment as on rehabilitation.
statements.note: About the main aim of prison: helping offenders return to society. Keeping prisons and sentences doesn't count against it.

statements.text: Traditional family structures are the foundation of a healthy society.
statements.agree: Traditional family structures are what a healthy society rests on.
statements.disagree: Traditional family structures are not the foundation of a healthy society.
statements.note: About whether the traditional family, such as a married mother and father raising their children, is what a healthy society rests on.

statements.text: Same-sex marriage should be legal.
statements.agree: Two people of the same sex can legally marry each other.
statements.disagree: The law should not extend marriage to same-sex couples.
statements.note: About legal marriage for same-sex couples, not civil unions. A religion's own rules on marriage are a different question.

statements.text: Abortion should be legal in most cases.
statements.agree: Women can legally choose to end most pregnancies.
statements.disagree: Abortion should be illegal in most cases.
statements.note: About whether women can legally end most pregnancies. Whether abortion is morally right is a different question.

statements.text: Religion should play a major role in public life.
statements.agree: Religious values and institutions should shape laws, schools and public life.
statements.disagree: Religion should not play a major role in public life.
statements.note: About religious values and institutions shaping laws, schools and public life. Religious people taking part in public life as individuals is not enough.

statements.text: Society should actively work to correct historical racial injustices.
statements.agree: Society should take active steps, such as targeted programs, to repair past discrimination.
statements.disagree: Society should not actively work to correct historical racial injustices.
statements.note: About society taking active steps, such as targeted programs, to repair past discrimination. Condemning past racism, or banning discrimination today, is not enough.

statements.text: Gender is primarily a social construct.
statements.agree: Ideas of what men and women are like come mostly from culture, not biology.
statements.disagree: Gender is not primarily a social construct.
statements.note: About whether ideas of what men and women are like come mostly from upbringing and culture rather than biology. Accepting some biological differences doesn't count against it.

statements.text: Preserving national cultural heritage is important.
statements.agree: Keeping a nation's inherited culture alive, including its language, customs and traditions, matters.
statements.disagree: Preserving national cultural heritage is not important.
statements.note: About the value of cultural continuity. A nation need not have its own state, and its heritage need not be uniform or unchanging. This does not require preserving every custom, state enforcement of culture or excluding foreign influences.

statements.text: Social reform should proceed in small steps.
statements.agree: Social reform should proceed in small steps.
statements.disagree: Social reform need not proceed in small steps.
statements.note: About whether social reform should proceed in small steps rather than big sudden changes. Whether a particular reform is wanted at all is a different question.

statements.text: Immigration should be tightly restricted.
statements.agree: The country should impose strict limits on immigration.
statements.disagree: Immigration should not be tightly restricted.
statements.note: About strict limits on how many people may immigrate. Having some border rules is not the same as tight restrictions.

statements.text: The United Nations should have powers to enforce its decisions against member states.
statements.agree: The UN should have authority to compel member states to comply with its decisions.
statements.disagree: The UN should have no authority to compel member states to comply with its decisions.
statements.note: Enforcement includes coercive measures such as sanctions; this does not necessarily require a world government or an independent UN army. Funding, advisory work and a larger voice in debate are separate from enforcement authority.

statements.text: Free trade benefits everyone in the long run.
statements.agree: Fewer tariffs and trade barriers make all countries better off over time.
statements.disagree: Free trade does not benefit everyone in the long run.
statements.note: About whether removing tariffs and other trade barriers leaves all countries better off over time. Some industries or workers losing out in the short run doesn't count against it.

statements.text: My country should put its own interests ahead of global cooperation.
statements.agree: A country should put its own interests ahead of cooperating with the rest of the world.
statements.disagree: My country should not put its own interests ahead of global cooperation.
statements.note: About a country putting its own interests ahead of cooperating with other countries. Cooperating where it also helps the country doesn't count against it.

statements.text: Military intervention abroad is never necessary to protect human rights.
statements.agree: Using military force in other countries is never necessary to protect people's human rights, even to stop a massacre.
statements.disagree: Military intervention abroad is sometimes necessary to protect human rights.
statements.note: About whether military force abroad is ever needed to protect human rights, for example to stop a massacre. Opposing particular interventions, or interventions by particular powers, is a different question.

statements.text: National borders should eventually be open.
statements.agree: In the long run people should be free to live and work in any country.
statements.disagree: National borders should not eventually be open.
statements.note: About whether, in the long run, people should be free to live and work in any country. Wanting more immigration than today is not enough.

statements.text: Economic growth should be limited to protect the environment.
statements.agree: Protecting nature can mean accepting less economic growth.
statements.disagree: Economic growth should not be limited for the sake of the environment.
statements.note: About accepting less economic growth when that is what protecting nature takes. Wanting cleaner growth with no loss of output is not enough.

statements.text: Climate change requires drastic government action.
statements.agree: Climate change calls for drastic action by governments.
statements.disagree: Climate change does not require drastic government action.
statements.note: About drastic government action to deal with climate change. Believing climate change is real, or wanting modest measures, is not enough.

statements.text: Technological progress will solve most of humanity's problems.
statements.agree: Science and technology will fix most of what goes wrong for people.
statements.disagree: Technology will not solve most of humanity's problems.
statements.note: About whether science and technology will fix most of what goes wrong for people. Believing technology helps with some problems is not enough.

statements.text: Governments should support the construction of nuclear power plants.
statements.agree: Government should support building nuclear power plants.
statements.disagree: Governments should not support construction of nuclear power plants.
statements.note: About government backing for building nuclear power plants, for example through funding or permits. Letting existing plants keep running is not enough.

statements.text: Revolution is never justified to achieve political change.
statements.agree: Overthrowing a government by revolution is never justified, whatever the cause.
statements.disagree: At least some revolutions have been justified.
statements.note: Whether any revolution can be justified, not whether a movement prefers reform for itself.

statements.text: Experts should have more say in policy than the general public.
statements.agree: Specialists should have more weight in decisions than public opinion.
statements.disagree: Experts should not have more say in policy than the general public.
statements.note: About giving specialists more weight than public opinion in deciding policy. Consulting experts before elected officials decide is not enough.

statements.text: A centrally planned economy is able to outperform a market economy.
statements.agree: An economy whose production is directed by a central plan is capable of working better than an economy directed by market exchange.
statements.disagree: A centrally planned economy is not able to outperform a market economy.
statements.note: About the performance of an economy run through central planning, not simply government regulation, public ownership of a few industries or planning one project. It asks whether central planning is capable of superior economic performance, not whether every plan succeeds or whether planning is always morally preferable.

statements.text: A market economy should be made up of worker-owned businesses.
statements.agree: Firms should compete in markets, but be owned by the people who work in them.
statements.disagree: A market economy should not be made up of worker-owned businesses.
statements.note: About market socialism with worker ownership: businesses still compete, but their workers own them instead of private investors. State ownership with markets, as in China, is a different model.

statements.text: A tax on the value of land should replace most other taxes.
statements.agree: Taxing the value of land, not work or trade, should fund most of government.
statements.disagree: A tax on land value should not replace most other taxes.
statements.note: About taxing land itself, by what a plot is worth regardless of what is built on it, instead of taxing wages, sales or profits.

statements.text: Large inheritances should be heavily taxed.
statements.agree: Large inheritances should be taxed heavily.
statements.disagree: Large inheritances should not be heavily taxed.
statements.note: About heavy taxes on large inheritances. Taxing income or wealth in general is a different question.

statements.text: Every adult should receive an unconditional basic income from the state.
statements.agree: Every adult gets a regular payment from the state, whether or not they work.
statements.disagree: Every adult should not receive an unconditional basic income from the state.
statements.note: About a regular payment from the state to every adult, with no conditions such as work or need. Benefits only for the poor or unemployed are not enough.

statements.text: Tariffs should protect domestic industry from foreign competition.
statements.agree: Taxes on imports should shield domestic producers from foreign competition.
statements.disagree: Tariffs should not be used to protect domestic industry from foreign competition.
statements.note: About taxes on imports meant to shield domestic producers from foreign competition. Tariffs used only to raise revenue are a different question.

statements.text: The state should direct investment toward strategic industries.
statements.agree: The government should steer money into industries it considers important.
statements.disagree: The state should not direct investment toward strategic industries.
statements.note: About industrial policy: the state backing industries it sees as key, such as energy, chips or steel.

statements.text: Property should be widely distributed among small owners.
statements.agree: Property should belong to many people in small holdings.
statements.disagree: Property should not be widely distributed among small owners.
statements.note: About the desired distribution of property across society. Small holdings include family farms, shops and workshops. No particular redistribution method is specified.

statements.text: Money should eventually be abolished.
statements.agree: Eventually people should produce and share without money.
statements.disagree: Money should not eventually be abolished.
statements.note: About a future society where goods are shared without money. Abolishing wage labour is a separate statement.

statements.text: A free market in money should replace central banking.
statements.agree: Central banks should give way to a market in which people choose the money they use without a central bank controlling its supply.
statements.disagree: A free market in money should not replace central banking.
statements.note: About replacing central banking with market provision of money. Simply closing one central bank, adopting another state's currency, or abolishing money itself is a different position.

statements.text: State-recognized collective bargaining bodies should set wages.
statements.agree: Officially recognized bodies representing employers and workers should negotiate wages together.
statements.disagree: State-recognized collective bargaining bodies should not set wages.
statements.note: About joint wage-setting in officially recognised bodies, without a separate role in setting product prices.

statements.text: A party with the right ideology should have the exclusive right to lead the state.
statements.agree: One ideologically correct party should hold state leadership without competing parties having a right to replace it.
statements.disagree: No party's ideology should give it an exclusive right to lead the state.
statements.note: Exclusive leadership is different from winning repeated competitive elections. Subordinate allied parties need not be banned, but they lack a right to replace the leading party. No particular ideology is named as correct.

statements.text: A hereditary monarch is acceptable as a ceremonial head of state.
statements.agree: It is acceptable for a king or queen who inherits the throne to be the country's symbolic head while others govern.
statements.disagree: A hereditary monarch is not acceptable as a ceremonial head of state.
statements.note: About a monarch who reigns without governing, as in today's constitutional monarchies. A ruler with real power passing it to their child is a separate statement.

statements.text: Democracy is the best form of government, even when voters choose badly.
statements.agree: Democracy is best even when voters make poor choices.
statements.disagree: Democracy is not the best form of government when voters choose badly.
statements.note: About whether democracy is the best form of government even when voters make poor choices. Disliking one election result doesn't count against it.

statements.text: Citizens should decide major laws in direct votes.
statements.agree: Major laws should be decided by citizens voting on them themselves.
statements.disagree: Major laws should not be decided by direct votes of citizens.
statements.note: Direct votes include referendums and popular assemblies; this is not merely electing representatives or approving an exceptional constitutional change.

statements.text: Workers' councils should replace parliaments as the basis of political power.
statements.agree: Political power should rest on councils elected in workplaces in place of parliaments.
statements.disagree: Workers' councils should not replace parliaments as the basis of political power.
statements.note: About councils of delegates elected in workplaces, like the soviets of the early Russian revolution, as the basis of government.

statements.text: Regions should have the right to secede from the country.
statements.agree: Regions should be able to leave the country.
statements.disagree: Regions should have no right to secede from the country.
statements.note: About whether regions should be able to leave the country. Wanting more self-government within the country is not enough.

statements.text: Some people are naturally better suited to rule than others.
statements.agree: Some people are better suited by nature to govern.
statements.disagree: Some people are not naturally better suited to rule than others.
statements.note: About whether some people are better suited by nature to govern. Skills gained through training or experience are a different question.

statements.text: Political violence is never justified.
statements.agree: Violence is never an acceptable way to pursue political goals.
statements.disagree: Political violence is sometimes justified.
statements.note: About whether violence is ever an acceptable way to pursue political goals. Ordinary self-defence is a different question.

statements.text: War strengthens a nation's character.
statements.agree: War develops virtues in a nation, such as courage and discipline.
statements.disagree: War does not strengthen a nation's character.
statements.note: A general character-building claim, not a claim that every war is beneficial. Honouring soldiers, accepting necessary defence and noting one incidental benefit are distinct from this claim.

statements.text: The state should be strictly separate from religion.
statements.agree: Government should maintain a strict institutional separation from religion.
statements.disagree: The state should not be strictly separate from religion.
statements.note: About institutional separation, not whether religious people may hold personal beliefs or participate in public debate.

statements.text: Laws should be based on religious scripture.
statements.agree: Laws should follow religious texts.
statements.disagree: Laws should not be based on religious scripture.
statements.note: About taking the law from holy books, such as the Bible or the Quran (for example sharia law). Laws that merely happen to match religious teaching are not enough.

statements.text: Private companies should replace state courts.
statements.agree: Courts should be run as private businesses in place of a public court system.
statements.disagree: Private companies should not replace state courts.
statements.note: A proposal for replacing the court system, not merely allowing private arbitration alongside public courts.

statements.text: My country should be militarily stronger than its rivals.
statements.agree: My country's military strength should exceed that of its rivals.
statements.disagree: My country should not seek greater military strength than its rivals.
statements.note: This concerns superiority, not merely adequate defence, parity, high spending or a larger domestic arms industry. It does not assert that the country currently has superiority.

statements.text: A nation should be made up mainly of one ethnic group.
statements.agree: A nation should be mainly one ethnic people.
statements.disagree: A nation should not be made up mainly of one ethnic group.
statements.note: About whether a country should belong mainly to one people of shared ancestry, rather than to all its citizens alike.

statements.text: Class conflict is the main driving force of history.
statements.agree: History is mainly driven by conflict between economic classes.
statements.disagree: Class conflict is not the main driving force of history.
statements.note: About whether history moves mainly through struggles between classes, such as lords and peasants or owners and workers. Believing classes exist, or that some conflicts were class-based, is not enough.

statements.text: Society should aim for equality of outcomes.
statements.agree: Society should aim for people to end up with broadly equal material conditions.
statements.disagree: Equality of outcomes should not be society's goal.
statements.note: A goal of substantial equality, not identical lives or a claim that every individual must receive the same reward. Equal opportunity alone does not meet this goal.

statements.text: Indigenous peoples should have authority over their traditional lands.
statements.agree: Indigenous peoples should control their traditional territories.
statements.disagree: Indigenous peoples should not have authority over their traditional lands.
statements.note: About indigenous peoples controlling their traditional lands, for example deciding how the land is used. Recognising past wrongs, or a right to be consulted, is not enough.

statements.text: Former colonial powers owe reparations to the nations they colonized.
statements.agree: Countries that had colonies should compensate the countries they colonized.
statements.disagree: Former colonial powers do not owe reparations to the nations they colonized.
statements.note: About whether countries that had colonies owe compensation to the countries they colonised. An apology alone is not enough.

statements.text: Nations belonging to the same civilization should form a political union.
statements.agree: Countries within one civilization should unite politically.
statements.disagree: Nations belonging to the same civilization should not form a political union.
statements.note: Political union means shared political institutions, not friendly relations or cultural cooperation. A civilization can be defined by a shared religion, such as the Islamic world.

statements.text: Pursuing your own self-interest is morally good.
statements.agree: Looking after your own interests is right, not just allowed.
statements.disagree: Pursuing your own self-interest is not morally good.
statements.note: About whether putting your own interests first is a virtue rather than something merely tolerated, as Ayn Rand argued.

statements.text: Citizens' duties to their community come before their individual rights.
statements.agree: What you owe your community matters more than your personal rights.
statements.disagree: Citizens' duties to their community do not come before their individual rights.
statements.note: About which comes first when they clash: what you owe your community, or your personal rights.

statements.text: Nature has value in itself, apart from its usefulness to humans.
statements.agree: Nature matters for its own sake, not only because it is useful to people.
statements.disagree: Nature does not have value in itself, apart from its usefulness to humans.
statements.note: About whether forests, rivers and wildlife matter for their own sake, even if people gain nothing from them.

statements.text: Population growth should be actively limited.
statements.agree: Population growth should be deliberately held down.
statements.disagree: Population growth should not be actively limited.
statements.note: About measures to slow population growth, for example family-planning campaigns or limits on family size.

statements.text: Industrial civilization has been a disaster for humanity.
statements.agree: Industrial society has done more harm than good to humanity.
statements.disagree: Industrial civilization has not been a disaster for humanity.
statements.note: About whether factories, machines and modern industry have, on the whole, harmed humanity.

statements.text: Society should speed up technological change even if it disrupts existing institutions.
statements.agree: Speed up technological change even if it upends existing institutions.
statements.disagree: Society should not speed up technological change if it disrupts existing institutions.
statements.note: About pushing new technology, such as AI, ahead as fast as possible even if existing institutions are upended.

statements.text: Adults should be free to enhance themselves with technology.
statements.agree: Adults may use technology to improve their bodies and minds.
statements.disagree: Adults should not be free to enhance themselves with technology.
statements.note: About using technology, such as gene editing, implants or drugs, to make people stronger, smarter or longer-lived.

statements.text: Governments should delegate some final decisions to AI systems.
statements.agree: AI systems should make some government decisions without a human official approving each decision.
statements.disagree: Human officials should retain final approval over every government decision involving AI.
statements.note: This concerns authority to decide, not software that supplies advice, analysis or paperwork. Human oversight of system design is distinct from approval of each decision.

statements.text: People should be able to use encryption the government cannot break.
statements.agree: People should be able to keep their communications private, even from government.
statements.disagree: People should not be able to use encryption the government cannot break.
statements.note: About encryption, which scrambles messages so only the intended reader can read them, and whether police must have a way in.

statements.text: Restoring a lost social order matters more than pursuing progress.
statements.agree: Recovering how society used to be matters more than moving forward.
statements.disagree: Restoring a lost social order does not matter more than pursuing progress.
statements.note: About whether bringing back an older way of life, such as older social roles or forms of rule, matters more than progress.

statements.text: Policies should be judged on their results regardless of whether they fit an ideology.
statements.agree: Judge policies by what they achieve, independently of whether they match an ideology.
statements.disagree: Whether a policy fits an ideology should count independently of its results.
statements.note: About judging a policy by what it achieves, not by whether it fits a set of beliefs. Weighing results alongside ideology is not enough.

statements.text: Direct action should replace electoral politics as the way to achieve political change.
statements.agree: People seeking political change should act directly—for example, with strikes, boycotts or occupations—instead of pursuing change through elections and parliaments.
statements.disagree: Direct action should not replace electoral politics as the way to achieve political change.
statements.note: About using direct action, such as strikes, boycotts, blockades and occupations, instead of elections and lawmaking. Using direct action alongside voting is not enough.

statements.text: The methods used to change society should reflect the society one wants to create.
statements.agree: You can't reach a free, fair society by unfree or unfair means.
statements.disagree: The methods used to change society should not reflect the society one wants to create.
statements.note: About whether the methods used to change society should reflect the society one aims for, for example democratic means for a democratic goal. Whether the goal is worth pursuing is a different question.

statements.text: Humanity would be better off returning to a hunter-gatherer way of life.
statements.agree: Humanity would be better off living as hunter-gatherers again.
statements.disagree: Humanity would not be better off returning to a hunter-gatherer way of life.
statements.note: About whether humanity would be better off living as hunter-gatherers again. Wanting a simpler or less industrial life is not enough.

statements.text: The division of labor should be abolished.
statements.agree: Work should no longer be divided into separate specialized jobs held by different people.
statements.disagree: The division of labor should not be abolished.
statements.note: About whether each person should do one specialised job, or everyone should take part in many kinds of work.

statements.text: Goods should ultimately be distributed according to each person's needs.
statements.agree: In the society we should aim for, a person's needs should determine their share of goods.
statements.disagree: Goods should not ultimately be distributed according to each person's needs.
statements.note: About the eventual principle of distribution, not merely a safety net within a system of wages and property.

statements.text: Meeting people's needs should replace making a profit as the purpose of production.
statements.agree: Production should be organised to provide what people need, instead of being organised around what yields a profit.
statements.disagree: Meeting people's needs should not replace making a profit as the purpose of production.
statements.note: About what guides production throughout the economy, including services. This is stronger than regulating profitable businesses or providing a safety net. It does not specify who should own production, require a central state plan, or prescribe a distribution rule. It concerns profit as the organising purpose, not simply whether any enterprise ever records an accounting surplus.

statements.text: Profit made from owning businesses comes from exploiting the workers who produce it.
statements.agree: Owners' profit is value taken from workers' labor.
statements.disagree: Profit made from owning businesses does not come from exploiting the workers who produce it.
statements.note: About whether owners' profit is value taken from the labor of the workers who produce it. Unfair pay or bad conditions at some firms is not enough.

statements.text: After a revolution, the working class should hold dictatorial power over the former ruling classes until classes disappear.
statements.agree: A workers' state must suppress the old ruling class for a time.
statements.disagree: After a revolution, the working class should not hold dictatorial power over the former ruling classes until classes disappear.
statements.note: About the working class holding dictatorial power over the former owners and rulers after a revolution, until classes disappear. A revolution alone is a different question.

statements.text: Collective farms should replace individually operated farms.
statements.agree: Farming should be organized as joint cultivation by groups of farmers instead of separate individual farm operations.
statements.disagree: Collective farms should not replace individually operated farms.
statements.note: About how cultivation is organized, not merely who owns the land. A collective farm pools the farming operation; a purchasing or marketing cooperative of otherwise separate farms does not by itself qualify. Collective farming need not be state-owned or compulsory. This asks which form should replace the other, without prescribing force or a timetable.

statements.text: Capitalism inevitably causes wars between great powers.
statements.agree: Wars between great powers are an unavoidable consequence of capitalism.
statements.disagree: Capitalism does not inevitably cause wars between great powers.
statements.note: About whether great-power war is unavoidable under capitalism, not merely whether economic interests contribute to some wars.

statements.text: Taxation is theft.
statements.agree: Taking people's earnings by force is wrong, whatever it pays for.
statements.disagree: Taxation is not theft.
statements.note: About whether taxation is legitimate at all, not whether some taxes are too high.

statements.text: The state should restrict what adults do only to prevent harm to others.
statements.agree: Choices that harm no one else should never be crimes.
statements.disagree: The state may restrict what adults do for reasons other than preventing harm to others.
statements.note: About laws against things that harm only the person doing them, or offend others, such as drug use or not wearing a seatbelt.

statements.text: Rights belong exclusively to individuals.
statements.agree: Individuals hold rights; groups have no rights of their own beyond the rights of their members.
statements.disagree: Groups have rights of their own.
statements.note: This concerns whether a human group itself holds rights, for example a nation, community or association. Individuals exercising their rights together are different from a group holding an independent right.

statements.text: The government should be able to conscript citizens into military service.
statements.agree: The government should be able to require citizens to serve in the military.
statements.disagree: Military service should always be voluntary.
statements.note: About whether the government may require citizens to serve in the military, as in a draft. Encouraging voluntary service is a different question.

statements.text: The freedom to leave a country is a more important check on government than the right to vote.
statements.agree: People keep governments honest best by being able to leave.
statements.disagree: The freedom to leave a country is not a more important check on government than the right to vote.
statements.note: About which keeps governments in check better: people's freedom to move away, or their vote.

statements.text: Government should be run on business principles.
statements.agree: The state should be managed the way a well-run business is: watching costs and judged on results.
statements.disagree: Government should not be run on business principles.
statements.note: About applying business methods, such as efficiency, cost control and competition, to running a country.

statements.text: Freedom requires the material means to exercise it.
statements.agree: Being free requires having the practical resources to act on one's choices, such as an adequate livelihood.
statements.disagree: Freedom does not require the material means to exercise it.
statements.note: About the meaning of freedom, not a particular method of providing resources.

statements.text: Cultural elites hold more political power than elected officials.
statements.agree: The people who run the press, universities and other cultural institutions have more real power than the people voters elect.
statements.disagree: Cultural elites do not hold more political power than elected officials.
statements.note: About where power really lies. Cultural elites means those who shape opinion, such as journalists, academics and editors.

statements.text: Average differences in ability between racial groups are largely genetic.
statements.agree: Group differences in ability are mostly inherited.
statements.disagree: Average differences in ability between racial groups are not largely genetic.
statements.note: About whether average ability differences between racial groups are mostly inherited. Differences between individuals within a group are a different question.

statements.text: Organized social groups should replace political parties as the basis of representation.
statements.agree: People should gain political representation through social bodies such as families, local communities and occupational associations instead of political parties.
statements.disagree: Organized social groups should not replace political parties as the basis of representation.
statements.note: About the basis of seats in governing institutions, not merely consulting associations or letting them lobby elected parties. The social groups meant here are existing social communities and associations, not parties renamed as groups. It does not require every example to receive a separate seat.

statements.text: The state should direct every area of life.
statements.agree: Every part of life should be subject to state direction.
statements.disagree: Some areas of life should remain outside state direction.
statements.note: About comprehensive state direction of life, not simply a powerful government.

statements.text: The nation needs a radical rebirth to overcome a period of decadence.
statements.agree: The nation has decayed and must be reborn.
statements.disagree: The nation does not need a radical rebirth to overcome decadence.
statements.note: About whether the nation has decayed and needs a radical rebirth. Wanting ordinary reforms is not enough.

statements.text: A strong nation should expand its territory.
statements.agree: Great nations grow, including by gaining territory.
statements.disagree: A strong nation should not expand its territory.
statements.note: About a strong nation gaining more territory, for example by annexation or conquest. Defending or keeping its existing borders is not enough.

statements.text: Political authority should rest on personal oaths of loyalty binding followers to their lords.
statements.agree: A lord's political authority should be grounded in the personal loyalty sworn by followers.
statements.disagree: Political authority should not rest on personal oaths of loyalty binding followers to their lords.
statements.note: About oath-bound lordship as a foundation of political authority. General loyalty to a leader, an oath to uphold a constitution and a patronage network without oaths are different. The statement does not require a particular land-tenure arrangement.

statements.text: Farmers should be legally forbidden to leave the estates they work.
statements.agree: People farming an estate should lack the legal freedom to leave that estate.
statements.disagree: Farmers should have the legal freedom to leave the estates they work.
statements.note: This concerns legal attachment to an estate. It does not itself require labour dues to a lord, prohibit selling a particular landholding, impose a duty to cultivate all owned land or describe ordinary notice periods in freely terminable jobs. Economic difficulty moving is not a legal prohibition.

statements.text: No knowledge is neutral: what a society counts as true reflects who holds power in it.
statements.agree: What gets treated as fact or expert knowledge reflects the interests of whoever has power, not a neutral search for truth.
statements.disagree: Some knowledge is neutral.
statements.note: About whether what a society treats as true or expert knowledge is shaped by those in power, so that none of it is neutral. Some bias in some fields is not enough.

statements.text: Some moral truths hold across all cultures.
statements.agree: Some things are right or wrong for everyone, in every culture and era.
statements.disagree: No moral truths hold across all cultures.
statements.note: About whether at least some moral rules apply to everyone, in every culture and era. How such truths are known, by reason or by revelation, is a different question.

statements.text: Politics should put a reasoned common good ahead of bargaining among competing groups.
statements.agree: Politics should prioritise a single common good identified by reasoning over compromises among organised interests.
statements.disagree: Politics should not put a reasoned common good ahead of bargaining among competing groups.
statements.note: A reasoned common good means a good for society as a whole that reasoning can identify. "Ahead of" asks priority, not whether every compromise must be forbidden.

statements.text: The Jewish people have a right to a state of their own in the Land of Israel.
statements.agree: Jews, as a people, are entitled to a country of their own in the Land of Israel.
statements.disagree: The Jewish people do not have a right to a state of their own in the Land of Israel.
statements.note: About whether Jews, as a people, have a right to their own state in the Land of Israel. How that state should treat its neighbours or its minorities is a different question.

statements.text: Members of a nation's diaspora should have the right to settle in its ancestral homeland.
statements.agree: People belonging to a nation but living abroad should be entitled to settle in that nation's ancestral homeland.
statements.disagree: Members of a nation's diaspora should not have a general right to settle in its ancestral homeland.
statements.note: This concerns a right of settlement, not automatic citizenship, encouragement to emigrate, a requirement to move, annexation of territories where related people already live or permission to seize someone else's private property. Diaspora members include descendants born abroad; the claim does not mean only people who personally emigrated.

statements.text: A national language that has fallen out of everyday use should be revived as the language of the state.
statements.agree: A national language that has fallen out of everyday use should be brought back as the language of the state.
statements.disagree: A national language that has fallen out of everyday use should not be revived as the language of the state.
statements.note: About bringing back a national language that people no longer use every day and making it the official language of the state, as with Hebrew or Irish. Merely teaching or protecting the language is not enough.

statements.text: Workers should have a democratic vote in how large companies are run.
statements.agree: Employees should have voting rights in the management of large companies.
statements.disagree: Workers should not have democratic voting rights in the management of large companies.
statements.note: About employees having a vote on how large companies are run, such as seats on the board. Voting on union representation is a different question, and ownership need not change.

statements.text: Parents should receive public vouchers to spend on any school they choose.
statements.agree: Public education money follows the child to whichever school the family picks.
statements.disagree: Parents should not receive public vouchers to spend on any school they choose.
statements.note: About public money for schooling going to parents as vouchers they can spend at any school, including private ones. Letting families choose among state-run schools only is not the same.

statements.text: Governments should avoid running large budget deficits to stimulate the economy.
statements.agree: Governments should not borrow heavily, spending much more than they collect in taxes, to boost the economy.
statements.disagree: Governments may borrow heavily, spending much more than they collect in taxes, to boost the economy.
statements.note: About whether governments should borrow heavily to boost a weak economy, for example in a recession. Wanting low taxes or small government is a different question.

statements.text: Political freedom cannot last without economic freedom.
statements.agree: Free citizens need the freedom to own property, trade and choose work, or political freedom cannot last.
statements.disagree: Political freedom can last without economic freedom.
statements.note: About whether political freedom can survive without economic freedom, meaning the freedom to own property, trade and choose work. Liking free markets for their own sake is not enough.

statements.text: Government should rely more on its rulers' moral example than on legal enforcement.
statements.agree: Government should depend more on leaders setting a good example than on enforcing laws with penalties.
statements.disagree: Government should rely at least as much on legal enforcement as on its rulers' moral example.
statements.note: About whether government should depend more on rulers setting a good moral example than on enforcing laws with penalties. Abolishing law is not what it asks.

statements.text: Every people that sees itself as a nation has the right to a state of its own.
statements.agree: A people with a shared national identity is entitled to its own self-governing state.
statements.disagree: Not every people that sees itself as a nation has the right to a state of its own.
statements.note: About whether every people that sees itself as a nation has a right to its own state. Respecting the borders of existing countries is a different question.

statements.text: My country should be willing to use force abroad without approval from the UN Security Council.
statements.agree: A country can act militarily on its own judgment even if the UN does not authorize it.
statements.disagree: My country should not be willing to use force abroad without approval from the UN Security Council.
statements.note: About whether a country should be willing to use military force abroad even when the UN Security Council has not approved it. Whether any particular war is justified is a different question.

statements.text: Reason is more important than religious faith.
statements.agree: Where they conflict, evidence and reasoning should count for more than faith, God, revelation or scripture.
statements.disagree: Reason is not more important than religious faith.
statements.note: About whether, where they conflict, evidence and reasoning should count for more than religious faith. Whether tradition, feeling or will should guide us is a different question.

statements.text: Welfare benefits should be reserved for citizens.
statements.agree: Only citizens should be eligible for welfare benefits, including immigrants who have become citizens.
statements.disagree: Non-citizens should also be eligible for welfare benefits.
statements.note: About citizenship as an eligibility requirement; priority for citizens is a weaker claim than exclusive eligibility.

statements.text: People able to work should have to work to receive welfare benefits.
statements.agree: People who are able to work should have to work in order to receive welfare benefits.
statements.disagree: People able to work should be eligible for welfare benefits without a work requirement.
statements.note: About working as a condition of receiving welfare benefits, not merely a general duty to contribute.

statements.text: Partnership between the classes should take priority over class struggle.
statements.agree: Employers and workers should treat each other as partners whose cooperation comes before conflict, even where their interests differ.
statements.disagree: Partnership between the classes should not take priority over class struggle.
statements.note: About relations between social classes, chiefly employers and workers: whether they are partners or opponents. It is not about whether every dispute or strike should be prohibited.

statements.text: Cultural heritage that holds back new creation should be destroyed.
statements.agree: Old museums, libraries and institutions matter less than room for the new, and may be swept away.
statements.disagree: Cultural heritage that holds back new creation should not be destroyed.
statements.note: About whether old cultural heritage, such as museums, libraries and institutions, may be destroyed when it holds back new creation. Merely preferring new art is not enough.

statements.text: Countries that see themselves as dominated by the leading Western powers should form a common front against them.
statements.agree: Countries that feel dominated by Western powers should band together to resist them.
statements.disagree: Countries that see themselves as dominated by the leading Western powers should not form a common front against them.
statements.note: About whether countries that feel dominated by leading Western powers should band together to resist them. Simply disliking Western influence is not enough.

statements.text: Workers should put national solidarity ahead of international class solidarity.
statements.agree: Workers' solidarity with their own nation should take priority over solidarity with workers across borders.
statements.disagree: Workers should not put national solidarity ahead of international class solidarity.
statements.note: This is a priority between forms of solidarity, not a prohibition on all international cooperation or on national unions.

statements.text: The law should reflect different public roles for each sex.
statements.agree: The law should give men and women different roles in public life.
statements.disagree: The law should not reflect different public roles for each sex.
statements.note: About legal differences in public roles, not simply different family responsibilities or personal preferences.

statements.text: Lending money at interest should be prohibited by law.
statements.agree: Charging interest on loans is banned by law.
statements.disagree: Lending money at interest should be legal.
statements.note: About a legal ban on lending money at interest. Disliking high interest rates or capping them is not the same.

statements.text: The law should enforce racial segregation in everyday public life.
statements.agree: Law should require people of different races to use separate public spaces, such as schools and public facilities.
statements.disagree: The law should not enforce racial segregation in everyday public life.
statements.note: Includes compulsory separation of racial groups in residential and public settings. Voluntary separation or different sovereign states alone does not satisfy this claim.

statements.text: The state is essentially a tool by which the ruling class dominates the others.
statements.agree: Laws, police and government mainly serve the interests of whoever owns the economy and holds power.
statements.disagree: The state is not essentially a tool by which the ruling class dominates the others.
statements.note: About whether the state, with its laws, police and government, mainly serves the interests of those who own the economy. Believing the state is sometimes biased is not enough.

statements.text: New fossil fuel extraction should be allowed.
statements.agree: New oil and gas wells and coal mines should be permitted.
statements.disagree: New fossil fuel extraction should not be allowed.
statements.note: About permitting new oil, gas and coal production, such as new wells and mines. Keeping existing production going is a different question.

statements.text: Immigrants should replace their original culture with the national culture.
statements.agree: Newcomers should adopt the host nation's culture in place of their original culture.
statements.disagree: Immigrants should not be expected to replace their original culture with the national culture.
statements.note: This concerns cultural replacement, not learning a common language or respecting laws while retaining a distinct heritage.

statements.text: Elites are deliberately promoting mass immigration to replace the native population.
statements.agree: Powerful elites deliberately encourage mass immigration with the aim of replacing the native population.
statements.disagree: Elites are not deliberately promoting mass immigration to replace the native population.
statements.note: About an alleged intention behind immigration policy, not demographic change alone.

statements.text: Legislative seats should be allocated to parties in proportion to the votes they receive.
statements.agree: A party with a fifth of the votes gets about a fifth of the seats.
statements.disagree: Legislative seats should not be allocated to parties in proportion to the votes they receive.
statements.note: About giving parties legislative seats in proportion to their share of the votes, so a party with a fifth of the votes gets about a fifth of the seats. Having several parties under another system is not the same.

statements.text: My country should treat spreading its form of government abroad as a special national mission.
statements.agree: Spreading our political system abroad should be a special calling of our nation.
statements.disagree: Spreading its form of government abroad should not be a special national mission of my country.
statements.note: About whether a country should treat spreading its own form of government abroad as a special calling. Simply being proud of its system is not enough.

statements.text: Society is organized in a way that systematically advantages men over women.
statements.agree: Laws, institutions and customs still favor men over women.
statements.disagree: Society is not organized in a way that systematically advantages men over women.
statements.note: About whether laws, institutions and customs systematically favor men over women today. Some individual cases of sexism are not enough.

statements.text: Most politicians put their own interests before those of ordinary people.
statements.agree: Most people in political office look after themselves first and the public second.
statements.disagree: Most politicians do not put their own interests before those of ordinary people.
statements.note: A general claim about politicians, not about one government, party or regime. Self-serving need not mean breaking the law.

statements.text: The state should discourage people with inherited disabilities from having children.
statements.agree: Public policy, such as sterilization or incentives, should reduce the passing on of inherited disabilities.
statements.disagree: The state should not discourage people with inherited disabilities from having children.
statements.note: About whether the state should steer who has children. Preventing them by law is a stronger form of discouraging.

statements.text: Governments should face legal accountability for their security forces' past abuses.
statements.agree: Governments should answer in law for past abuses by their security forces, including unlawful killings.
statements.disagree: Governments should not face legal accountability for their security forces' past abuses.
statements.note: About government responsibility in law for past abuses, not merely criticism, an inquiry or an apology.

statements.text: Government should exist solely to protect people from physical violence.
statements.agree: A government should exist, with protection against physical violence as its only task.
statements.disagree: Government should not exist solely to protect people from physical violence.
statements.note: About a minimal government whose only task is protecting people from force, such as police, courts and defence. Wanting a smaller state that still does other things is not enough.

statements.text: Starting families across racial lines should be discouraged.
statements.agree: People of different races should be discouraged from forming a family together, whether through marriage or having children.
statements.disagree: Starting families across racial lines should not be discouraged.
statements.note: About whether people of different races should be discouraged from marrying or having children together. Personal preference about whom to marry is a different question.

statements.text: All people should have equal rights before the law.
statements.agree: The law should treat everyone as an equal, whatever their birth, sex, race or status.
statements.disagree: Not all people should have equal rights before the law.
statements.note: About equality before the law. Equal moral worth is not the question: many traditions affirm it while defending legal rank.

statements.text: Lasting socialism in one country requires socialist revolutions abroad.
statements.agree: Socialism in a single country will not endure without successful socialist revolutions in other countries.
statements.disagree: Lasting socialism in one country does not require socialist revolutions abroad.
statements.note: About whether socialism's endurance requires revolutions elsewhere, not whether the first revolutionary victory occurs in one country or whether international solidarity is desirable.

statements.text: A state created by settlement from abroad that displaced the existing population is a colonial project.
statements.agree: Settling a land and displacing its people is colonialism, whatever the settlers' motives.
statements.disagree: A state created by settlement from abroad that displaced the existing population is not a colonial project.
statements.note: About whether a state founded by settlers from abroad who displaced the existing population counts as colonialism. Whether that state should now continue to exist is a different question.

statements.text: All citizens should be governed by the same civil laws regardless of their religion.
statements.agree: Marriage, inheritance and family law are the same for everyone, not set by each religious community.
statements.disagree: All citizens should not be governed by the same civil laws regardless of their religion.
statements.note: About whether marriage, inheritance and family law should be the same for everyone, rather than set by each religious community. A religion's own rules for its members in private life are a different question.

statements.text: Religious conversion should be restricted by law.
statements.agree: The law limits or polices changing religion, for example to prevent pressure or inducement.
statements.disagree: Religious conversion should be free of legal restriction.
statements.note: About laws that limit or police changing religion, for example to prevent pressure or inducement. Social disapproval of conversion is not the same.

statements.text: The slaughter of cattle should be banned by law.
statements.agree: Killing cows and similar cattle is outlawed.
statements.disagree: The slaughter of cattle should be legal.
statements.note: About a legal ban on killing cows and similar cattle, often because they are held sacred. Rules on how animals are slaughtered are a different question.

statements.text: State schools should not provide religious instruction.
statements.agree: State schools should not teach religion.
statements.disagree: State schools may provide religious instruction.
statements.note: About whether state schools should teach religion as part of their instruction. Teaching about religions as a subject of study is a different question.

statements.text: A socialist state surrounded by hostile countries should pursue a policy of strengthening state power.
statements.agree: A socialist state surrounded by hostile countries should pursue a policy of strengthening state power.
statements.disagree: A socialist state surrounded by hostile countries should not pursue a policy of strengthening state power.
statements.note: About whether a socialist state surrounded by hostile countries should build up state power instead of letting it fade away. Strengthening defence alone is not enough.

statements.text: Political authority needs the consent of the governed to be legitimate.
statements.agree: Rulers have a right to rule only because the people they rule have agreed to it.
statements.disagree: Consent of the governed is not the only basis of legitimate political authority.
statements.note: About whether a government's right to rule depends on the agreement of the people it governs. Holding elections is not the same.

statements.text: A country should aim to export more than it imports.
statements.agree: A country should try to sell more abroad than it buys from abroad.
statements.disagree: A country should not aim to export more than it imports.
statements.note: About whether a country should aim to sell more abroad than it buys. Having a surplus by chance is not the same as aiming for one.

statements.text: Governments have the right to expel a minority seen as hostile.
statements.agree: A state may force a minority it sees as hostile to leave the country.
statements.disagree: Governments do not have the right to expel a minority seen as hostile.
statements.note: Expelling includes pressure that leaves no real choice, not voluntary emigration or moving people within the country.

statements.text: It is always wrong to be the first to use force, whatever the goal.
statements.agree: Starting the use of force against someone, or against their property, is wrong whatever it is meant to achieve.
statements.disagree: It is not always wrong to be the first to use force, whatever the goal.
statements.note: Force used in defence is outside this claim. Taking or damaging someone's property by force counts as using force.

statements.text: Struggle between peoples is the main engine of human progress.
statements.agree: Rivalry and conflict between nations or peoples do more than anything else to drive humanity forward.
statements.disagree: Struggle between peoples is not the main engine of human progress.
statements.note: About struggle between peoples or nations as the main driver of human progress. Competition between individuals or firms in a market is a different question.

statements.text: Parties that seek to abolish the constitutional order should be banned.
statements.agree: A government should outlaw political parties that aim to do away with its constitutional order.
statements.disagree: Parties that seek to abolish a country's constitutional order should be free to organize.
statements.note: About banning parties that aim to overthrow the country's whole system of government, as Germany's constitution allows.

statements.text: Living under someone else's arbitrary power is a loss of freedom, even without actual interference.
statements.agree: A person loses freedom from being at another person's mercy, even if that power is never exercised.
statements.disagree: Unused arbitrary power over a person does not itself reduce that person's freedom.
statements.note: About whether living at someone else's mercy costs a person freedom even if that power is never used. Actual interference is a different question.

statements.text: Political power should be divided among separate bodies that check one another.
statements.agree: Political power should be split among separate branches and levels that can each limit the others.
statements.disagree: Political power should not be divided among separate bodies that check one another.
statements.note: About whether political power should be divided among separate branches and levels that can each limit the others. Having elections alone is not enough.

statements.text: Workers need a disciplined party of committed revolutionaries to lead them.
statements.agree: Workers require political leadership from a tightly organised revolutionary party.
statements.disagree: Workers do not need a disciplined revolutionary party to lead them.
statements.note: This is a political prescription for workers' leadership, not a prediction about whether workers spontaneously become revolutionary.

statements.text: Public policy should give first priority to the needs of the poor.
statements.agree: Meeting poor people's needs should be the first consideration in public policy.
statements.disagree: Public policy should not give first priority to the needs of the poor.
statements.note: About giving poor people priority in public decisions, beyond treating poverty as one concern among many.

statements.text: Council tenants should have a legal right to buy their homes.
statements.agree: People who rent their homes from the council should be able to buy them by right.
statements.disagree: Council tenants should not have a legal right to buy their homes.
statements.note: About whether tenants of publicly owned homes, called council homes in Britain, have a legal right to buy them. Whether new public housing should be built is a different question.

statements.text: The law should restrict strikes.
statements.agree: There should be legal limits on strike action.
statements.disagree: The law should impose no restrictions on strikes.
statements.note: About whether the law should put limits on strikes, with no particular ballot rule required. Having rules on how a strike is run is not the same as banning strikes.

statements.text: Population growth is the main cause of lasting poverty.
statements.agree: Population growth is the leading explanation of persistent poverty.
statements.disagree: Population growth is not the main cause of lasting poverty.
statements.note: About whether population growth is the leading cause of lasting poverty. Population growth being one factor among others is not enough.

statements.text: Ethnic diversity weakens social cohesion.
statements.agree: A society holds together less well when its members belong to different ethnic groups.
statements.disagree: Ethnic diversity does not weaken a society's ability to hold together.
statements.note: Ethnic diversity means communities distinguished by ancestry or cultural heritage, including what is often called race.

statements.text: Lotteries among citizens should replace elections for public office.
statements.agree: Citizens should be selected at random for public office in place of being elected.
statements.disagree: Lotteries among citizens should not replace elections for public office.
statements.note: This concerns the general method of selecting officeholders. It does not merely propose an advisory citizens' assembly, random jury selection, rotation in office or a lottery within an otherwise electoral selection process. Rejection does not imply support for elections: appointment and hereditary succession are other alternatives.

statements.text: During a national emergency, governments should be allowed to suspend ordinary legal protections to defeat internal enemies.
statements.agree: A national emergency sometimes justifies temporarily withdrawing normal legal safeguards against people the government regards as internal enemies, such as protections against detention without trial.
statements.disagree: Governments should not be allowed to suspend ordinary legal protections to defeat internal enemies, even during a national emergency.
statements.note: About permission to suspend normal safeguards during an emergency, not a requirement to do so in every emergency. Suspension might itself be authorised by a constitution; agreement does not require rejecting every legal limit or permitting every abuse. “Internal enemies” means those the government identifies as threats from within the country, not a judgment that its designation is correct.

statements.text: Governments should fix maximum prices for essential foods in times of scarcity.
statements.agree: Governments should set legal price ceilings on essential foods when supplies are scarce.
statements.disagree: Governments should not fix maximum prices for essential foods, even in times of scarcity.
statements.note: About legal ceilings on the prices of essential foods when supplies are scarce. Handing out food aid or subsidies is a different question.

statements.text: The government should control the news media.
statements.agree: The people in power should decide what the country's news media publish.
statements.disagree: The government should not control the news media.
statements.note: About political control over what news media publish, whether by a party, a king or a junta, with or without state ownership. Ordinary regulation such as libel law is not the same.

statements.text: The ruling party should command the armed forces.
statements.agree: The governing party's own leadership should control the armed forces.
statements.disagree: The ruling party should not command the armed forces.
statements.note: About military command belonging to a party organisation, not merely to officeholders who belong to the governing party.

statements.text: Immigrants should need at least ten years of residence to qualify for citizenship.
statements.agree: Eligibility for citizenship should require immigrants to have lived in the country for ten years or longer.
statements.disagree: Immigrants should qualify for citizenship with less than ten years of residence.
statements.note: This concerns the residence requirement for ordinary naturalisation, not entry visas, permanent residence, birthright citizenship, descent-based citizenship or processing delays. Other eligibility requirements are outside this statement.

statements.text: Elected representatives should be paid no more than an average worker.
statements.agree: Those who hold public office are paid no more than an average worker.
statements.disagree: Elected representatives may be paid more than an average worker.
statements.note: About capping pay for elected representatives at an average worker's pay. Paying them a modest salary above that is not enough.

statements.text: Party members should be required to carry out decisions adopted after internal debate.
statements.agree: After members debate and adopt a party decision, every member should have to help implement it, including those who opposed it.
statements.disagree: Party members should not be required to carry out decisions adopted after internal debate.
statements.note: About binding implementation of party decisions, rather than a ban on all criticism or unconditional obedience to a leader.

statements.text: Nations should pool part of their sovereignty in a supranational union such as the European Union.
statements.agree: Countries should hand part of their decision-making power to a union of nations, such as the European Union.
statements.disagree: Nations should not hand part of their decision-making power to a union of nations, such as the European Union.
statements.note: About whether countries should hand part of their decision-making power to a union of nations, such as the European Union. Ordinary treaties and trade deals are not the same.

statements.text: The head of state should hold effective command of the armed forces.
statements.agree: Real authority to command the military should rest with the head of state.
statements.disagree: The head of state should not hold effective command of the armed forces.
statements.note: Effective command is distinct from a ceremonial title. Legislative oversight can coexist with it.

statements.text: Bishops should govern the national church.
statements.agree: The national church should have episcopal government, with its bishops holding governing authority.
statements.disagree: Bishops should not govern the national church.
statements.note: About episcopal church government, not legal establishment, bishop selection, state supremacy over churches or a prohibition on consultative synods.

statements.text: Senior religious scholars should hold the highest political authority.
statements.agree: The most senior religious scholars should have the highest authority over the state and its laws.
statements.disagree: Senior religious scholars should not hold the highest political authority.
statements.note: About whether the most senior religious scholars should hold final authority over the state and its laws. Religion influencing politics without clerics holding the top office is not enough.

statements.text: In a war between rival great powers, working people should work for their own government's defeat.
statements.agree: During a war between rival great powers, workers should actively seek their own government's defeat.
statements.disagree: In a war between rival great powers, working people should not work for their own government's defeat.
statements.note: About actively seeking the defeat of one's own government in a war between rival great powers. Refusing military service or opposing a war does not alone establish this aim.

statements.text: Art should be censored to protect citizens' moral character.
statements.agree: Art, poetry and stories that harm people's moral character should be censored.
statements.disagree: Art should not be censored for its effect on people's moral character.
statements.note: About whether art, poetry and stories that harm people's moral character should be censored. Censorship for other reasons, such as security, is a different question.

statements.text: A president should be allowed to stand for re-election without limit.
statements.agree: A president should be free to stand for re-election as many times as they like.
statements.disagree: A president should be limited in how many times he or she may stand for re-election.
statements.note: About whether a president may stand for re-election as many times as they like. A single long term is a different question.

statements.text: Voters should be able to remove elected officials from office before their term ends.
statements.agree: Voters should be able to remove elected officials before their terms end.
statements.disagree: Elected officials should serve out their full terms.
statements.note: About whether voters can remove elected officials before their term ends. Voting them out at the next election is not enough.

statements.text: A country should stay out of permanent military alliances.
statements.agree: A country should stay out of permanent military alliances.
statements.disagree: A country should not rule out permanent military alliances.
statements.note: About whether a country should stay out of permanent military alliances. Stationing troops abroad is a different question.
