statements.text: Renting out housing should be prohibited.
statements.agree: No housing provider, including a private owner or the state, should charge rent for a home.
statements.disagree: Renting out housing should be permitted in at least some circumstances.
statements.note: This asks about a complete prohibition of housing rent. It does not require individual home ownership, prescribe common ownership, prohibit cost-free occupancy or address rental of farmland and business premises.

statements.text: A professional army should be replaced by an armed citizenry.
statements.agree: Defense should rest with armed ordinary citizens, not a standing force.
statements.disagree: A professional army should not be replaced by an armed citizenry.
statements.note: About replacing a professional army with ordinary citizens trained to fight and keeping arms. Adding a citizen reserve to a standing army is not enough.

statements.text: Rural life is morally healthier than life in cities.
statements.agree: Life in the countryside is morally healthier than life in cities.
statements.disagree: Rural life is not morally healthier than life in cities.
statements.note: About whether life in the countryside makes people morally better than life in cities. Preferring rural scenery or lifestyle is not enough.

statements.text: A nation divided between states by a border drawn by an outside power should be reunified as one state.
statements.agree: A people split by an imposed border should be brought together in a single state.
statements.disagree: A nation divided between states by a border drawn by an outside power should not be reunified as one state.
statements.note: About whether a nation split between states by a border an outside power drew should become one state again, as with Korea or Germany before 1990. Closer cooperation across the border is not enough.

statements.text: University-educated people tend to be out of touch with the realities of ordinary life.
statements.agree: People with advanced schooling are cut off from how ordinary people live and work.
statements.disagree: University-educated people are not especially out of touch with the realities of ordinary life.
statements.note: About whether people with a university education tend to be cut off from how ordinary people live. Disagreeing with their views is not enough.

statements.text: No culture is superior to another.
statements.agree: Cultures do not rank above one another in overall worth.
statements.disagree: Some cultures are superior to others.
statements.note: Cultures here includes the broad cultural traditions often called civilizations. Comparing particular practices or technologies is distinct from ranking whole cultures.

statements.text: The state should be able to execute people convicted of the gravest crimes, such as terrorism.
statements.agree: The worst crimes can be punished by death.
statements.disagree: The state should be barred from executing people convicted of the gravest crimes, such as terrorism.
statements.note: About whether the state may execute people convicted of the gravest crimes, such as terrorism. Support for harsh prison sentences is a different question.

statements.text: School curricula should include sex education.
statements.agree: Schools should teach pupils about sex.
statements.disagree: School curricula should exclude sex education.
statements.note: About including sex education in schools; the statement does not specify a curriculum model.

statements.text: Public schools should teach creationism alongside evolution in science lessons.
statements.agree: Public school science classes should present creationist accounts of origins alongside evolutionary explanations.
statements.disagree: Public schools should not teach creationism alongside evolution in science lessons.
statements.note: About creationism in public science lessons, not studying creation beliefs in comparative religion, teaching intelligent design alone or replacing evolution entirely.

statements.text: Pornography should be restricted by law.
statements.agree: The law should limit the making or sale of pornography.
statements.disagree: Pornography should be free of legal restriction.
statements.note: About laws that limit the making or sale of pornography. Personal disapproval of it is not enough.

statements.text: Citizenship at birth should go only to children of citizens.
statements.agree: Children of citizens are citizens wherever they are born; being born in the country is not enough.
statements.disagree: Citizenship at birth should not go only to children of citizens.
statements.note: About who becomes a citizen at birth. Also giving it to children of permanent residents, or to everyone born in the country, means disagreeing.

statements.text: Governments should support the public use of minority languages.
statements.agree: Public institutions should help minority languages be used in public life, for example through teaching or services in those languages.
statements.disagree: Governments should not support the public use of minority languages.
statements.note: About public support for minority languages, beyond leaving their private use unrestricted.

statements.text: Members of religious minorities should be exempt from general laws that burden their religious practice.
statements.agree: Believers can be excused from rules, such as dress or work-day rules, that conflict with their faith.
statements.disagree: Religious minorities should not be exempt from general laws that burden their practice.
statements.note: About excusing believers from general laws that burden their religious practice, such as dress or work-day rules. Freedom to hold beliefs is a different question.

statements.text: Unconventional ways of living should be encouraged.
statements.agree: People should be encouraged to live in ways that differ from social custom.
statements.disagree: Unconventional ways of living should not be encouraged.
statements.note: About actively encouraging people to live in unconventional ways. Merely allowing them to is not enough.

statements.text: Poor countries' foreign debts should be cancelled.
statements.agree: The foreign debts of poor countries should be written off, ending their obligation to repay them.
statements.disagree: Poor countries' foreign debts should not all be cancelled.
statements.note: This concerns cancellation of poor countries' external public debts, not household debts, postponing payments, refinancing or reducing interest. Cancellation does not necessarily mean a unilateral default or prohibit compensation to creditors from another source.

statements.text: Political independence means little without economic transformation.
statements.agree: Political independence means little unless the economic and property system is also transformed.
statements.disagree: Political independence means a great deal even without economic transformation.
statements.note: About former colonies and dependent countries: whether formal independence is enough, or the economy inherited from colonial rule must also change.

statements.text: The constitution should be written by a democratically elected constituent assembly.
statements.agree: An assembly elected by the people for that purpose should draft the constitution.
statements.disagree: The constitution should not be written by a democratically elected constituent assembly.
statements.note: About who should write a constitution: an elected assembly, or a ruler, parliament or appointed body. Whether the current constitution should be replaced is a separate question.

statements.text: Rapid economic development justifies temporary restrictions on political freedom.
statements.agree: Temporary limits on political freedom are justified to achieve rapid economic development.
statements.disagree: Rapid economic development does not justify temporary restrictions on political freedom.
statements.note: Concerns justification of a temporary trade-off for economic development, not whether repression and growth have ever coexisted.

statements.text: Wealthy countries have a duty to give substantial aid to the world's poor, wherever those people live.
statements.agree: Distance and nationality do not weaken the duty of the rich to help the poor abroad.
statements.disagree: Wealthy countries have no duty to give substantial aid to the world's poor abroad.
statements.note: About whether wealthy countries have a duty to give substantial aid to poor people abroad, whatever their nationality or distance. Giving aid when it suits national interest is not enough.

statements.text: My country should have nuclear weapons under its independent control.
statements.agree: My country should possess its own nuclear arsenal with independent authority over its use.
statements.disagree: My country should not have nuclear weapons under its independent control.
statements.note: About national control of nuclear weapons. An independent arsenal is compatible with alliances and foreign technical cooperation; hosting an ally's weapons alone does not establish independent national control.

statements.text: The head of state should be chosen in a direct popular election.
statements.agree: Voters themselves should elect the head of state, without an intermediary body selecting the officeholder.
statements.disagree: The head of state should not be chosen in a direct popular election.
statements.note: The head of state is distinct from a prime minister or other head of government. Direct election describes the selection method; this statement does not add universal suffrage, competitive-party or executive-power requirements.

statements.text: Central banks should set monetary policy independently of elected governments.
statements.agree: Elected governments should leave central banks free to make monetary-policy decisions within their legal mandates.
statements.disagree: Central banks should not set monetary policy independently of elected governments.
statements.note: About operational independence in monetary policy. The law can still define the bank's mandate and require public accountability. This does not specify price stability as its main goal or require private ownership.

statements.text: A country should not give up land it claims as its historic homeland in exchange for peace agreements.
statements.agree: Land claimed as the historic homeland is not traded away, even for peace.
statements.disagree: A country may give up land it claims as its historic homeland in exchange for peace agreements.
statements.note: About refusing to give up land a country claims as its historic homeland in return for peace. Wanting peace in general is a different question.

statements.text: Private property is justified only to the extent that it serves the common good.
statements.agree: Private ownership is legitimate only insofar as it benefits society.
statements.disagree: Private property does not need to serve the common good to be justified.
statements.note: Concerns whether social benefit is necessary for justifying private ownership; it does not say social benefit is sufficient.

statements.text: The Soviet Union was a state-capitalist society.
statements.agree: The Soviet economy was capitalist under state ownership, with the state taking the place of private capitalists.
statements.disagree: The Soviet Union was not a state-capitalist society.
statements.note: About whether the Soviet economy worked like capitalism with the state as the single owner and employer, rather than workers controlling production. Calling it a failure or a dictatorship is not enough.

statements.text: Governments should act on environmental risks even before there is scientific certainty that harm will occur.
statements.agree: Lack of full certainty is no reason to delay protective action.
statements.disagree: Governments should not act on environmental risks before there is scientific certainty that harm will occur.
statements.note: About acting to prevent possible environmental harm before science has confirmed it, such as restricting a chemical on early warning signs. Waiting until harm is proven is a different position.

statements.text: An armed attack on one allied country should be treated as an attack on all of them.
statements.agree: Allies are bound to defend one another against armed attack.
statements.disagree: An armed attack on one allied country should not be treated as an attack on all of them.
statements.note: About mutual-defence pacts, such as NATO's promise that an attack on one member is an attack on all. Helping an ally in some other way, or only agreeing to consult, is not enough.

statements.text: A territory annexed without the consent of its people remains under unlawful occupation.
statements.agree: A territory annexed without its people's consent is still under unlawful occupation.
statements.disagree: A territory annexed without the consent of its people does not remain under unlawful occupation.
statements.note: About land that a state takes over and declares its own against its people's will, for example Crimea or Western Sahara. Whether the land should be handed back is a different question.

statements.text: Religious institutions should operate under the government's authority.
statements.agree: The government should have authority over religious institutions' internal affairs.
statements.disagree: Religious institutions should be independent of government direction in their internal affairs.
statements.note: This goes beyond ordinary laws that apply to everyone. It concerns government supervision of religious bodies themselves, such as appointing clergy.

statements.text: A head of state should stand above party politics as a symbol of national unity.
statements.agree: The nation's figurehead is non-partisan and belongs to everyone.
statements.disagree: A head of state should not stand above party politics as a symbol of national unity.
statements.note: About the head of state staying out of party politics and standing for the whole nation, as a ceremonial monarch or president might. Whether the head of state is elected, or holds real powers, is a different question.

statements.text: Military force is a legitimate way for a country to prevent a region from leaving it.
statements.agree: A country has the right to stop a region becoming independent by using its military.
statements.disagree: Military force is not a legitimate way for a country to prevent a region from leaving it.
statements.note: About the legitimacy of military force to retain territory, not merely its practical effectiveness. Agreement does not require using force first or in every case; disagreement does not rule out defending people against attacks for a separate reason.

statements.text: A region should be free to retain its economic system upon joining a larger state.
statements.agree: Joining a larger state should leave a region free to keep its existing economic arrangements.
statements.disagree: A region should not be free to retain its economic system upon joining a larger state.
statements.note: Concerns a distinct economic system within a shared state, not simply regional tax rates. Legal-system continuity and the overall degree of self-government are separate questions. This is a proposed institutional entitlement, not a claim that autonomy is feasible in every case.

statements.text: The head of state should be regarded as sacred.
statements.agree: The person holding the highest state office should be treated as holy.
statements.disagree: The head of state should not be regarded as sacred.
statements.note: About sacred status for the ruler personally, not ordinary respect, legal immunity, divine ancestry or the sacredness of the state.

statements.text: Income tax should have a single percentage rate.
statements.agree: The same income-tax percentage should apply across taxable income levels.
statements.disagree: Income tax should not have a single percentage rate.
statements.note: About a single statutory rate of income tax. An exempt minimum does not create a second positive rate. Tax deductions, credits, the size of the rate and replacing income tax entirely are separate questions.

statements.text: A person's character comes more from their environment than from innate nature.
statements.agree: A person's character comes more from their environment than from innate nature.
statements.disagree: Innate nature shapes a person's character at least as much as their environment does.
statements.note: About whether upbringing, society and experience shape a person's character more than inborn traits do. Accepting that some traits are inborn doesn't count against it.

statements.text: The ruler should be above the law.
statements.agree: The ruler should not be bound by the laws that he or earlier rulers made.
statements.disagree: The ruler should not be above the law.
statements.note: About exemption from the country's own laws, not freedom from divine or natural law.

statements.text: Expanding humanity into space should be a central goal of civilization.
statements.agree: Civilization should aim to spread into space.
statements.disagree: Expanding humanity into space should not be a central goal of civilization.
statements.note: About spreading humanity beyond Earth, such as settling other planets, as one of civilization's main aims. Supporting some space research is not enough.

statements.text: The best constitution combines rule by the few with rule by the many.
statements.agree: The best government combines a governing role for a few with a governing role for the wider population.
statements.disagree: The best constitution does not combine rule by the few with rule by the many.
statements.note: About combining elite and popular elements in government, such as a senate alongside a popular assembly. A government built on only one of them is not the same.

statements.text: Publicly honouring a national leader as the embodiment of the nation is acceptable.
statements.agree: It is acceptable to honour a national leader in public life as the embodiment of the nation, for example with portraits, statues and mass praise.
statements.disagree: Publicly honouring a national leader as the embodiment of the nation is not acceptable.
statements.note: About public leader worship, not ordinary appreciation of a leader's achievements. The claim permits this form of honour; it does not require it, demand every kind of monument, prescribe compulsory praise, or limit the question to a living incumbent.

statements.text: Courts should presume that children of separated parents spend equal time with each parent.
statements.agree: Equal shared parenting is the starting point unless there is a reason against it.
statements.disagree: Courts should not presume that children of separated parents spend equal time with each parent.
statements.note: About a default rule that children of separated parents spend equal time with each parent unless there is a reason against it. Courts deciding each case on its own facts is a different approach.

statements.text: Class struggle continues under socialism.
statements.agree: Conflicts between social classes persist after a society becomes socialist.
statements.disagree: Class struggle does not continue under socialism.
statements.note: About persistence of class conflict in a socialist society, not a demand to intensify it, an assertion of violent conflict or a claim that every self-described socialist state genuinely is socialist.

statements.text: Large landed estates should be transferred to the people who farm them, even against their owners' wishes.
statements.agree: The farmers who work large estates should take ownership from the landowners, with the transfer compulsory if owners refuse.
statements.disagree: Large landed estates should not be compulsorily transferred to the people who farm them.
statements.note: About land reform transferring ownership to cultivators, individually or through their farming cooperatives. It does not specify compensation, violent methods or state ownership. Public ownership with farmers only renting or using the land is a different arrangement.

statements.text: Refugees displaced during a conflict should have the right to return to their former homes.
statements.agree: People who became refugees during a conflict should be permitted to return to the homes they themselves left.
statements.disagree: A right to return to former homes should not apply to all refugees displaced during a conflict.
statements.note: This concerns the people personally displaced, whether they fled or were expelled. It asserts a right to choose return, not forced repatriation, a hereditary right for descendants, a right to acquire citizenship merely through ancestry or an obligation to return to unsafe conditions.

statements.text: A state has a rightful claim to land beyond its borders inhabited by people of its nationality.
statements.agree: The presence of people belonging to the same nation gives a state a legitimate territorial claim outside its borders.
statements.disagree: The presence of people of its nationality does not give a state a rightful claim to land beyond its borders.
statements.note: “Nationality” means belonging to a national people, not merely holding a passport or living abroad as an expatriate. This asks whether that presence grounds a territorial claim, not whether force should be used, whether every resident shares that nationality or whether other grounds for a claim exist.

statements.text: Leaving one's religion should be punishable by law.
statements.agree: Abandoning the faith is a crime that the state may punish.
statements.disagree: People must be free to leave their religion without legal penalty.
statements.note: About making it a crime, punished by the state, to leave one's religion. Social disapproval, or a religion's own rules for its members, is not the same.

statements.text: The law should require women to cover themselves fully in public.
statements.agree: The law requires women to cover themselves fully in public.
statements.disagree: The law should not require women to cover themselves fully in public.
statements.note: About a law forcing women to cover themselves fully in public, such as with a full veil. Women choosing to cover, or a ban on covering, is a different question.

statements.text: A single currency shared by several countries is better than separate national currencies.
statements.agree: A single currency shared by several countries is better than separate national currencies.
statements.disagree: A single currency shared by several countries is not better than separate national currencies.
statements.note: About several countries sharing one currency, such as the euro. Fixing exchange rates between separate currencies is not the same.

statements.text: Ethnically related peoples should unite in a single state.
statements.agree: Peoples who share an ethnic heritage, such as the Slavic, Arab or Turkic peoples, should come together in one state, even across present borders.
statements.disagree: Ethnically related peoples should not unite in a single state.
statements.note: About one state for peoples bound by shared descent, language or culture. A league, federation of separate states or close cooperation does not count, nor does union on the basis of faith, class or a continent alone.

statements.text: National minorities should govern their own cultural affairs within the state they live in.
statements.agree: A national minority should run its own schools, language and cultural institutions inside the state it lives in.
statements.disagree: National minorities should not govern their own cultural affairs within the state they live in.
statements.note: Cultural affairs means schools, language and cultural institutions run by the minority, not merely government support for its language. Whether a minority should have its own state is a separate question.

statements.text: Persecuted minorities should prioritise seeking equal rights where they live over emigrating to establish a homeland.
statements.agree: Seeking equal rights in their countries of residence should take priority over leaving to establish a homeland as the response to persecution.
statements.disagree: Emigrating to establish a homeland should take at least as much priority as seeking equal rights where persecuted minorities live.
statements.note: This compares collective responses to persecution. It does not deny anyone the right to leave, require remaining in immediate danger or rule out pursuing both aims. Seeking a separate state on territory where a group already lives is not emigration.

statements.text: Changes to the economic structure of society are the main cause of historical change.
statements.agree: Changes in how society produces and exchanges goods explain historical change more than ideas or moral insight do.
statements.disagree: Changes to the economic structure of society are not the main cause of historical change.
statements.note: About the main cause of social and political change over history. Economic structure means how production and exchange are organised. Calling it the main cause allows ideas and political action to have effects too.

statements.text: The state should prohibit cartels.
statements.agree: Businesses should be legally barred from agreements with competitors to suppress competition, such as fixing prices.
statements.disagree: The state should not prohibit cartels.
statements.note: About prohibiting collusion among competing businesses, not breaking up large firms merely for their size, nationalising industry or banning ordinary trade associations.

statements.text: Failing companies should be left to fail.
statements.agree: Firms and banks bear the cost of their own failures, with no rescue from taxpayers.
statements.disagree: Failing companies should not always be left to fail.
statements.note: About refusing to rescue failing companies, including banks, with taxpayers' money. Helping the workers of a failed firm is a different question.

statements.text: A liberal democracy's institutions should not constrain the national majority's decisions.
statements.agree: Once the national majority has decided, public institutions, including courts and independent bodies, should not limit its decision.
statements.disagree: Public institutions should have the power to constrain a national majority's decisions in a liberal democracy.
statements.note: About institutional limits on the national majority, including constitutional review by courts. “Majority” means a democratic majority, not merely the largest ethnic group or a leader claiming to embody the people. Disagreement does not require courts to override every popular decision.

statements.text: Public bodies should be required to have roughly as many women as men.
statements.agree: Binding composition rules should ensure that public bodies have approximately equal numbers of women and men.
statements.disagree: Public bodies should not be required to have roughly as many women as men.
statements.note: About binding rules for the numbers of women and men in public decision-making bodies, such as assemblies, councils and public boards. A rule requiring only a smaller share of women, such as a third, does not count, nor does equal eligibility or a voluntary aim.

statements.text: A colonial empire should form a self-sufficient economic bloc closed to outside trade.
statements.agree: The mother country and its colonies should meet their economic needs within their own bloc instead of trading with the outside world.
statements.disagree: A colonial empire should not form a self-sufficient economic bloc closed to outside trade.
statements.note: About a closed imperial economy, not merely protecting domestic industries or reducing dependence on imports.

statements.text: International trade agreements should include binding labour standards.
statements.agree: Trade deals should impose legally binding requirements protecting workers.
statements.disagree: International trade agreements should not include binding labour standards.
statements.note: About labour obligations within trade agreements, not environmental clauses, domestic labour law alone or merely voluntary commitments.

statements.text: A sense of social duty should replace material rewards as the main motivation for work.
statements.agree: People should work mainly out of responsibility to society and a shared purpose, with personal material rewards playing a secondary role.
statements.disagree: Social duty should not take the place of material rewards as the main reason people work.
statements.note: About the principal motivation for work. Social duty includes service to others and commitment to a shared social purpose; material rewards include pay, bonuses and a share of profits. Agreement does not require eliminating all pay. This is a claim about the motivation that should predominate, not a prediction of how people currently behave or permission to force them to work.

statements.text: A small armed group is able to create the conditions for a wider revolution.
statements.agree: An armed minority's actions are capable of bringing about conditions that enable a broader revolutionary uprising.
statements.disagree: An armed minority's actions are incapable of bringing about the conditions for a broader revolutionary uprising.
statements.note: About the claim that initiating armed struggle helps create the conditions for a wider revolution, associated with Guevara's guerrilla strategy. It does not mean a group succeeds without any existing popular support, that it acts alone throughout the revolution, or that every armed attempt succeeds. Ability is distinct from whether this method is morally justified or preferable.

statements.text: Hereditary rank should be abolished.
statements.agree: Nobody should hold a special rank by birth, such as a noble title, a hereditary crown or a caste position, or the special rights attached to one.
statements.disagree: Hereditary rank should not be abolished.
statements.note: About status passed down by birth: noble titles, a hereditary crown, caste or estate rank, and the special rights attached to them, such as hereditary seats in a legislature. An inherited title counts even without material privilege. This is not about ordinary inheritance of property or wealth, earned honours, or private forms of address.

statements.text: School history lessons should centre on the student's own nation.
statements.agree: A student's own nation should be the main focus of school history lessons.
statements.disagree: A student's own nation should not be the main focus of school history lessons.
statements.note: About the main focus of history teaching. A nation need not have its own state. Including national history in a wider curriculum does not itself make it the centre.

statements.text: Advanced societies have the right to rule less advanced ones for a time to improve them.
statements.agree: Temporary rule by a more developed society is justified when it helps the ruled to progress.
statements.disagree: Advanced societies do not have the right to rule less advanced ones, even for a time to improve them.
statements.note: About temporary rule over other peoples for their supposed benefit, as in colonial 'civilizing missions'. Permanent domination for the rulers' own sake is a different claim.

statements.text: Schools should teach pupils to be patriotic.
statements.agree: Schools should cultivate patriotic feeling: loyalty to and pride in the nation, expressed for example through respect for its flag and anthem.
statements.disagree: Schools should not teach pupils to be patriotic.
statements.note: About patriotism as an educational goal, beyond learning facts about national history or symbols. It does not require unquestioning support for a government, compulsory ceremonies or claims that one's nation is superior. A nation need not have its own state.

statements.text: Race-based affirmative action should be abolished.
statements.agree: Admissions, hiring and contracts should not give preference to anyone because of their race.
statements.disagree: Race-based affirmative action should not be abolished.
statements.note: About ending preferences based on race in college admissions, hiring and government contracts. Helping poorer applicants of any race doesn't count against it.

statements.text: Only public institutions should create money.
statements.agree: Creating new money should be reserved to public institutions, excluding private banks' creation of money through lending.
statements.disagree: Money creation should not be reserved exclusively to public institutions.
statements.note: About a public monopoly on creating money, including deposit money, not merely issuing coins or banknotes, regulating banks or setting monetary-policy targets. Publicly owned banks remain possible.

statements.text: A general collapse of capitalism is avoidable.
statements.agree: Capitalism is not bound to suffer a general collapse.
statements.disagree: A general collapse of capitalism is unavoidable.
statements.note: About the inevitability of capitalism's general economic breakdown, not the absence of ordinary crises, moral approval of capitalism or immunity from deliberate replacement.

statements.text: Poor countries should end their economic ties with rich countries.
statements.agree: Poor countries should stop economic relations with wealthy countries.
statements.disagree: Poor countries should retain economic ties with rich countries.
statements.note: About poor countries cutting their trade, investment and lending ties with rich countries. Trading on better terms, or protecting some industries, is not the same.

statements.text: Most workers in wealthy countries benefit from the exploitation of poorer countries.
statements.agree: A majority of workers in rich countries gain material benefits from exploitation of poorer countries.
statements.disagree: At most half of workers in wealthy countries benefit from the exploitation of poorer countries.
statements.note: About most rich-country workers benefiting from exploitation abroad, not whether their own employers also exploit them.

statements.text: Private owners should have unrestricted legal freedom to choose whom they deal with.
statements.agree: Private owners should be free to refuse association, employment or service on any grounds, including discriminatory ones.
statements.disagree: Private owners' choice of whom they deal with should be subject to some restrictions.
statements.note: This concerns private freedom of association, including commercial dealings and employment. It is a legal freedom, not approval of prejudiced conduct.

statements.text: A written bill of rights that ordinary majorities cannot easily amend should limit government power.
statements.agree: Government should be bound by written guarantees of basic rights protected against easy amendment by ordinary majorities.
statements.disagree: Government should not be bound by a written bill of rights protected against easy amendment by ordinary majorities.
statements.note: About written rights guarantees that constrain government and are harder to change than ordinary laws. The rights need not be unchangeable. Disagreement could concern the written form, the special amendment protection, or using this kind of charter as a limit on government; it need not mean rejecting basic rights themselves.

statements.text: Colonial-era treaties that divided a people without consulting it have no binding force today.
statements.agree: Borders and treaties imposed by colonial powers without local consent can be set aside.
statements.disagree: Colonial-era treaties that divided a people without consulting it have binding force today.
statements.note: About whether treaties and borders imposed by colonial powers, without the consent of the people they divided, still bind today. Agreeing that they were unjust is not enough.

statements.text: The head of state should be elected.
statements.agree: An electorate should choose the head of state, either directly or through elected representatives.
statements.disagree: The head of state should not have to be chosen by election.
statements.note: About election to the head-of-state role, whether president or monarch. This does not specify who has the vote or require direct popular election.

statements.text: A decision should bind only those who consent to it.
statements.agree: Even a single dissenter should be free from a decision they have refused.
statements.disagree: Some decisions should bind people who have not consented to them.
statements.note: About whether decisions bind dissenters, including individual dissenters. This alone does not give a dissenter power to stop others acting.

statements.text: People have a right to resist rulers who violate the constitution.
statements.agree: People are entitled to resist a ruler's unconstitutional exercise of power.
statements.disagree: People have no right to resist rulers who violate the constitution.
statements.note: About a right of resistance to unconstitutional rule; resistance need not involve force or removal.

statements.text: Parliament should be the supreme lawmaking authority.
statements.agree: The representative legislature should have the final say on legislation.
statements.disagree: Parliament should not be the supreme lawmaking authority.
statements.note: About final legislative authority, including its relationship to the executive, courts, constitutional limits, royal assent and direct popular decisions. Parliamentary government alone does not establish supremacy.

statements.text: Animals are sentient beings whose suffering matters morally.
statements.agree: Animals can suffer, and that suffering counts in how we treat them.
statements.disagree: Animals are not sentient beings whose suffering matters morally.
statements.note: About whether animals can suffer and whether that suffering matters morally. Whether animals have the same rights as humans, or may be used for food, is a different question.

statements.text: Killing animals for food is morally acceptable under humane conditions.
statements.agree: It is morally acceptable to kill animals for food while minimising their suffering.
statements.disagree: Killing animals for food remains morally unacceptable even with suffering minimised.
statements.note: Humane conditions means minimising suffering, not assuming that killing itself is ethically justified. This concerns moral acceptance, not a legal obligation to eat meat. Research and nonlethal uses are separate questions.

statements.text: The wealthy have a duty to help people less fortunate than themselves.
statements.agree: Rich people have an obligation to help those worse off than they are.
statements.disagree: The wealthy have no duty to help people less fortunate than themselves.
statements.note: About a duty attached to wealth; this does not specify whether it should be enforced by law.

statements.text: A life withdrawn from public affairs is better than a life of political engagement.
statements.agree: Living privately away from public affairs is a better way to live than taking part in politics.
statements.disagree: A life withdrawn from public affairs is no better than a life of political engagement.
statements.note: About which way of life is preferable. Political engagement includes direct action and organising outside elections. The claim does not forbid private life or require everyone to hold office.

statements.text: Mass entertainment discourages people from challenging the existing social order.
statements.agree: Entertainment produced for mass audiences tends to weaken people's willingness to challenge the established social order.
statements.disagree: Mass entertainment does not generally discourage people from challenging the existing social order.
statements.note: This concerns a general social effect of mass entertainment, not every individual work, news reporting alone, a deliberate conspiracy by all producers or whether the existing order is good. It does not require endorsing censorship or denying that some popular art supports resistance.

statements.text: Public acceptance of ruling-class ideas is the main basis of that class's continued power.
statements.agree: The ruling class keeps its power mainly because people accept its ideas.
statements.disagree: Public acceptance of ruling-class ideas is not the main basis of that class's continued power.
statements.note: This is a description of the principal basis of class rule, not a statement that the rule is legitimate. Acceptance might be cultivated or taken for granted; it need not mean an informed free choice. Force may still contribute. Material dependence, obedience under threat and institutional participation are not automatically acceptance of ideas.

statements.text: The world economy's transfer of wealth from poor countries to rich countries keeps the poor countries poor.
statements.agree: The global economic system keeps poorer countries poor by directing their wealth toward richer countries.
statements.disagree: Transfers of wealth to richer countries do not explain poor countries' continuing poverty.
statements.note: A structural explanation of lasting poverty: profits, resources and surplus drained from poor countries through trade and investment, not simply that some wealth crosses borders.

statements.text: Public offices should be reserved for native-born citizens.
statements.agree: Only people born in the country should hold public office.
statements.disagree: Public offices should not be reserved for native-born citizens.
statements.note: About limiting public office to people born in the country, so that naturalized citizens are excluded. Requiring citizenship alone is not the same.

statements.text: Communist parties should determine their own strategies independently of foreign parties.
statements.agree: Each country's communist party should decide its strategy for socialism without taking orders from another country's party.
statements.disagree: Communist parties should not necessarily determine their strategies independently of foreign parties.
statements.note: Independence concerns authority to decide, not a ban on learning from foreign experience, voluntary cooperation or shared principles. This statement concerns communist parties specifically, not every socialist or social-democratic party. It does not assert that socialism succeeds in an isolated country.

statements.text: A poor country should rely more on its own resources for development than on foreign money.
statements.agree: A poor country should develop mainly with its own resources.
statements.disagree: A poor country should rely on foreign money at least as much as on its own resources.
statements.note: About whether a poor country's development should be paid for mainly from its own resources rather than foreign loans, aid and investment. Accepting some foreign help doesn't count against it.

statements.text: A country should demand the return of territory it lost to a neighbour in a past war.
statements.agree: Land lost in an old war can rightly be claimed back.
statements.disagree: A country should not demand the return of territory it lost to a neighbour in a past war.
statements.note: About a country demanding back land it lost to a neighbour in a past war. Regretting the loss is not enough.

statements.text: The descendants of a country's pre-colonial peoples should hold political leadership over the descendants of settlers.
statements.agree: Political leadership should belong to the country's original peoples.
statements.disagree: The descendants of a country's pre-colonial peoples should not hold political leadership over the descendants of settlers.
statements.note: About political leadership belonging to the descendants of a country's original peoples rather than to the descendants of settlers. Equal rights, or guaranteed representation, for indigenous peoples is not the same.

statements.text: Anti-fascism should be regarded as a founding value of a democratic constitution.
statements.agree: A democratic constitution should rest on rejecting fascism.
statements.disagree: Anti-fascism should not be regarded as a founding value of a democratic constitution.
statements.note: About a democratic constitution being founded on an explicit rejection of fascism. Banning particular parties or symbols is a different question.

statements.text: Communist one-party states deserve the same condemnation as fascist states.
statements.agree: Communist one-party regimes should be condemned as severely as fascist regimes.
statements.disagree: Communist one-party states should not receive the same condemnation as fascist states.
statements.note: About equal moral condemnation of the historical regimes, not whether their aims, class bases, institutions or every crime were identical.

statements.text: Slavery was not the main cause of the American Civil War.
statements.agree: The main cause of the American Civil War was something other than slavery.
statements.disagree: Slavery was the main cause of the American Civil War.
statements.note: About what the main cause of the American Civil War was, not whether slavery was wrong. Slavery being one of several causes is not the same as being the main one.

statements.text: Public monuments to widely condemned figures from a country's past should remain on public display.
statements.agree: Public monuments honouring widely condemned historical figures should stay publicly displayed rather than be removed from display.
statements.disagree: At least some public monuments to widely condemned historical figures should be removed from public display.
statements.note: This concerns continued public display of existing monuments, not flags, preserving an object in storage, building new memorials or destroying historical records. It permits explanatory material and does not claim that every figure deserves praise. The location and manner of display may still matter.

statements.text: Boys and men facing disadvantage in education, health and suicide deserve the same public attention and programmes as girls and women.
statements.agree: Boys and men who face disadvantage in education, health or suicide deserve as much public attention and as many programmes as girls and women.
statements.disagree: Boys and men facing disadvantage in education, health and suicide do not deserve the same public attention and programmes as girls and women.
statements.note: About boys and men facing disadvantage in education, health and suicide getting as much public attention and as many programmes as girls and women. Supporting a few programmes for them is not enough.

statements.text: Men experiencing domestic violence should have the same right to support services as women.
statements.agree: Abused men should have an equal entitlement to services supporting victims of domestic violence.
statements.disagree: Men experiencing domestic violence should have a different entitlement to support services from women.
statements.note: Equal entitlement does not mean identical services or equal total budgets regardless of need. This makes no claim about equal prevalence, average severity or the gender of the abuser, and does not exclude victims of other genders.

statements.text: Western political institutions are unsuitable for some civilizations.
statements.agree: Political institutions developed in the West are not a suitable model for every civilization.
statements.disagree: Western political institutions are suitable for every civilization.
statements.note: About the suitability of political institutions, not merely opposition to imposing them by force. A claim that one's own country prefers Western institutions does not say whether they suit every society.

statements.text: The armed forces should act as guardians of the constitutional order.
statements.agree: The military should have a political role in protecting the constitution and public order, stepping in when they are threatened.
statements.disagree: The armed forces should not act as guardians of the constitutional order.
statements.note: About a political role for the military, not ordinary defence duties or obedience to civilian orders.

statements.text: Unpaid work in the home should be paid.
statements.agree: Housework and care at home count as work and deserve wages.
statements.disagree: Unpaid work in the home should not be paid.
statements.note: About paying wages for housework and care at home, such as looking after children or a sick relative. Recognising such work as valuable is not enough.

statements.text: Adult children have a duty to care for their parents in need.
statements.agree: Grown children owe care to parents who need it.
statements.disagree: Adult children have no duty to care for their parents in need.
statements.note: About a duty of care to needy parents, not lifelong obedience, unconditional respect, ancestry worship or an exclusive requirement for daughters to provide unpaid care.

statements.text: Competitive examinations should determine recruitment to the civil service.
statements.agree: Civil servants should be recruited according to their performance in competitive examinations.
statements.disagree: Recruitment to the civil service should not depend on competitive examinations.
statements.note: This concerns administrative civil-service recruitment, not selecting elected political leaders, university admission, general merit language or tests that merely establish eligibility before another body chooses candidates. It does not prescribe the content of an exam or exclude accommodations and fair-access measures.

statements.text: Governments should block foreign companies from buying firms in strategic industries.
statements.agree: The state can stop foreign buyers from taking over key national businesses.
statements.disagree: Governments should not block foreign companies from buying firms in strategic industries.
statements.note: About the state stopping foreign companies from buying firms in strategic industries such as energy, ports or defence. Screening that never blocks a purchase is not enough.

statements.text: Adults should be free to end a marriage without having to prove fault.
statements.agree: Either spouse can leave a marriage without showing wrongdoing by the other.
statements.disagree: Ending a marriage should not be possible without proving fault.
statements.note: About ending a marriage without having to prove that a spouse did something wrong, such as adultery. Rules on dividing property or custody are different questions.

statements.text: Voters should be able to recall their elected representatives at any time.
statements.agree: Those who elected someone should be able to remove them before their term ends, whenever they choose.
statements.disagree: Voters should not be able to recall their elected representatives at any time.
statements.note: Recall is removal by the voters, not impeachment or waiting for the next election. Whether representatives must follow voters' instructions is a separate question.

statements.text: Privately managed individual savings accounts should replace state pensions funded from current workers' contributions.
statements.agree: Retirement benefits should come from each worker's own privately managed savings account in place of a state scheme using current contributions to pay current retirees.
statements.disagree: Privately managed individual savings accounts should not replace state pensions funded from current workers' contributions.
statements.note: About replacing a contribution-funded state pension system. Supplementary savings, partial diversion of contributions, state-managed individual accounts and a separate tax-funded minimum pension require distinct evidence.

statements.text: A person's right to hold land should end once they stop using it.
statements.agree: People should lose their right to a plot of land when they no longer use it.
statements.disagree: A person's right to hold land need not end when they stop using it.
statements.note: About losing the right to hold a plot of land once you stop using it, whoever holds the title. Taxing unused land is not the same.

statements.text: Government spending should require prior budget approval from an elected legislature.
statements.agree: An elected legislature must approve the government's budget before the government spends public money.
statements.disagree: Government spending should not require prior approval of the budget by an elected legislature.
statements.note: This is prior authorisation of spending, not merely consent to taxation or later scrutiny of accounts. "Legislature" includes a parliament or congress.

statements.text: One language should be the sole common language of public life, even where this restricts other languages.
statements.agree: The state should make one language the only common language of government, schooling and public life, limiting the use of others.
statements.disagree: One language should not be the sole common language of public life where this restricts other languages.
statements.note: About making one language the common language of government, schooling and public life. It does not require banning private use of other languages or the teaching of foreign languages.

statements.text: Foreigners should not be allowed to own land in the country.
statements.agree: Land stays in the hands of citizens; foreigners may not buy it.
statements.disagree: Foreigners should be allowed to own land in the country.
statements.note: About banning foreigners from owning land in the country. Limiting foreign ownership in some places, such as border areas, is not enough.

statements.text: A policy that produces unequal outcomes between racial groups should be treated as discriminatory, whatever its intent.
statements.agree: A policy whose results are unequal between racial groups counts as discriminatory, whatever was intended.
statements.disagree: A policy that produces unequal outcomes between racial groups should not be treated as discriminatory, whatever its intent.
statements.note: About judging discrimination by a policy's effect rather than its intent, for example a hiring test that one racial group fails more often. Disagreeing doesn't mean approving of intentional discrimination.

statements.text: The pursuit of ever more possessions does more harm than good.
statements.agree: Constantly seeking additional possessions is harmful overall, despite any benefits it brings.
statements.disagree: The pursuit of ever more possessions does not cause more harm than good overall.
statements.note: This concerns acquisitiveness as a way of life, not meeting unmet basic needs or whether consumer choices should be legal.

statements.text: My country should arm insurgents fighting governments it considers hostile.
statements.agree: My country should give weapons to foreign insurgents fighting governments it regards as enemies.
statements.disagree: My country should not arm insurgents fighting governments it considers hostile.
statements.note: About supplying weapons to foreign rebels, rather than political support alone.

statements.text: Great powers should have the right to send troops into allied countries against their governments' wishes to preserve those countries' political systems.
statements.agree: A great power should be entitled to intervene militarily without an allied government's consent to prevent its political system from being abandoned.
statements.disagree: Great powers should have no right to send troops against allied governments' wishes for the purpose of preserving those countries' political systems.
statements.note: This concerns permission to use troops to preserve an ally's political system, not a duty to intervene, preventing withdrawal from an alliance alone, humanitarian rescue, collective defence against an invasion or deployments accepted by the allied government.

statements.text: Corporate lobbying gives businesses excessive influence over government.
statements.agree: Businesses gain too much influence over government policy from their lobbying.
statements.disagree: Corporate lobbying does not give businesses excessive influence over government.
statements.note: Lobbying means trying to influence public decisions, including paid corporate representatives and in-house lobbyists. The claim is about excessive influence from that activity, not campaign donations alone, private wealth in general, corporate cultural power or a prescribed legal remedy.

statements.text: Governments should restrict foreign funding of domestic organizations.
statements.agree: The state should limit or screen money that foreign donors give to charities, campaign groups, the press and universities.
statements.disagree: Governments should not restrict foreign funding of domestic organizations.
statements.note: About the state limiting or screening money from abroad that goes to domestic charities, campaign groups, the press and universities. Banning foreign gifts to political parties alone is not enough.

statements.text: The state should give families financial incentives for having additional children.
statements.agree: Government payments or tax advantages should encourage families to have more children.
statements.disagree: The state should give families no financial incentives for having additional children.
statements.note: About financial encouragement of childbearing; this does not set an immigration policy.

statements.text: Local authorities should have the right to restrict home purchases to existing residents of their area.
statements.agree: A local authority should be permitted to reserve home purchases in its area for people who already live there.
statements.disagree: Local authorities should have no right to reserve home purchases in their area for existing residents.
statements.note: This asks about local legal authority to impose a residence requirement on buying homes, not merely giving local buyers priority. It does not prescribe using that power everywhere, restrict citizenship or ancestry, ban all second homes or prevent residents of foreign nationality from buying.

statements.text: Governments should guarantee a job to everyone willing to work, acting as employer of last resort.
statements.agree: The state offers public work to anyone who wants a job and cannot find one.
statements.disagree: Governments should not guarantee a job to everyone willing to work, acting as employer of last resort.
statements.note: About the state offering a public job to anyone willing to work who cannot find one. Unemployment benefits or job training alone is not enough.

statements.text: Spreading democracy brings peace.
statements.agree: More democracies means fewer wars, so promoting democracy serves peace.
statements.disagree: Spreading democracy does not bring peace.
statements.note: About whether the spread of democracy makes the world more peaceful, with fewer wars between states. Whether democracy is good in itself is a different question.

statements.text: A rule's legal status alone creates no moral duty to obey it.
statements.agree: The fact that something is law is not, by itself, a moral reason to obey it.
statements.disagree: Being the law gives a rule a moral claim to be obeyed.
statements.note: About whether being law creates a duty to obey. There may be other moral reasons to do what a particular law requires.

statements.text: Foreign powers have no right to intervene in a country's internal affairs, whatever the reason.
statements.agree: Outside governments have no entitlement to interfere in another country's internal affairs for any purpose.
statements.disagree: Foreign powers sometimes have a right to intervene in a country's internal affairs.
statements.note: Includes states acting collectively. This is an absolute prohibition on interference, not just opposition to wars of conquest.

statements.text: Industry-wide unions should replace craft unions.
statements.agree: Workers in the same industry should organise together regardless of their particular trade, replacing separate craft unions.
statements.disagree: Industry-wide unions should not replace craft unions.
statements.note: Craft unions organise a particular skilled trade. Industry-wide unions organise across trades within an industry. This does not require state control, compulsory membership or employer membership.

statements.text: A minority group is secretly conspiring against the nation.
statements.agree: A hidden minority plots against the nation and its people.
statements.disagree: No minority group is secretly conspiring against the nation.
statements.note: About conspiracy claims against an ethnic or religious minority as a whole, not wrongdoing by particular individuals.

statements.text: Legal recognition of marriage should be abolished.
statements.agree: Marriage should cease to be a legally recognised status.
statements.disagree: Marriage should retain legal recognition.
statements.note: About marriage as a distinct legal status. People would remain free to hold weddings and make ordinary private agreements. The claim does not abolish family life or general contract law.

statements.text: Everyone should have a legal right of access to government information.
statements.agree: Citizens have a legal right to see government information.
statements.disagree: Everyone should not have a legal right of access to government information.
statements.note: About a legal right for anyone to see government records, as freedom-of-information laws give. Voluntary openness, or access only for journalists, is not enough.

statements.text: Most goods should be produced close to where they are consumed.
statements.agree: The goods people consume should mainly come from nearby producers.
statements.disagree: Most goods need not be produced close to their place of consumption.
statements.note: About most goods, food included, being made close to where they are used. Some local production is not enough.

statements.text: Small informal groups of trusted people should replace permanent organizations in political struggle.
statements.agree: Small, informal, trust-based groups are the right form for political action, not lasting parties, unions or federations.
statements.disagree: Small informal groups of trusted people should not replace permanent organizations in political struggle.
statements.note: About small, trust-based groups taking the place of lasting parties, unions and federations in political action. Using informal groups alongside permanent organizations is not enough.

statements.text: A country's constitution should take precedence over international law.
statements.agree: A country's constitution should prevail when it conflicts with international legal obligations.
statements.disagree: A country's constitution should not automatically take precedence over international law.
statements.note: About constitutional primacy when the two conflict, not ignoring treaties whenever convenient.

statements.text: The national community should be defined by a shared religion.
statements.agree: Belonging to the nation goes with sharing its religion.
statements.disagree: The national community should not be defined by a shared religion.
statements.note: About whether sharing a religion is what makes someone part of the national community. A nation that merely has a majority religion is not the same.

statements.text: Weaker states should formally submit to a dominant power.
statements.agree: A weaker state should openly acknowledge a stronger power as its superior.
statements.disagree: Weaker states should not formally submit to a dominant power.
statements.note: Formal submission means acknowledging the dominant power's superiority, for example by tribute, homage or ritual. Following its lead in foreign policy is a separate question.

statements.text: Regions should keep most of the revenue they raise.
statements.agree: Regions should keep most of the revenue they raise.
statements.disagree: Regions should share at least half of the revenue they raise with other regions.
statements.note: About regions keeping most of the revenue raised within them, rather than sharing much of it with other regions. Giving regions more self-rule is a different question.

statements.text: Personal belongings should remain private under common ownership of production.
statements.agree: In an economy with common ownership of productive assets, people should still own their personal belongings.
statements.disagree: Common ownership of production need not leave personal belongings private.
statements.note: About people keeping personal belongings such as clothes and household goods as their own, even where farms and factories are commonly owned. Whether production should be commonly owned is a different question.

statements.text: Defeating communism should take priority over coexisting with it.
statements.agree: The political goal should be victory over communism ahead of accommodation with it.
statements.disagree: Defeating communism should not take priority over coexistence with it.
statements.note: Communism here refers to communist parties and one-party states, not Marx's proposed stateless society. Defeat does not necessarily mean war.

statements.text: Private companies should deliver publicly funded services.
statements.agree: Publicly funded services such as hospitals and schools should be run by private companies and charities as well as the state.
statements.disagree: Private companies should not deliver publicly funded services.
statements.note: About private companies and charities running publicly funded services such as hospitals and schools, alongside the state. The state paying for services is not enough.

statements.text: Religion offers illusory comfort for material suffering.
statements.agree: Religion gives people a false consolation for hardship in their material lives.
statements.disagree: Religion does not offer illusory comfort for material suffering.
statements.note: About whether religion offers a false comfort for hardship in people's material lives. Religion having other effects is a different question.

statements.text: Capitalism has been a historically progressive force that created the material basis for a better society.
statements.agree: Capitalism built the productive power and wealth that later and better societies rest on.
statements.disagree: Capitalism has not been a historically progressive force that created the material basis for a better society.
statements.note: About whether capitalism in the past built the productive wealth that a better society can rest on. Approving of capitalism today is a different question.

statements.text: Women's equality cannot be fully achieved without transforming the economic system.
statements.agree: Women's subordination is tied to how the economy is organised, so reform of laws and attitudes is not enough.
statements.disagree: Women's equality can be fully achieved without transforming the economic system.
statements.note: About whether full equality for women needs changes to how the economy is organised, beyond changes to laws and attitudes. Wanting economic change for other reasons is a different question.

statements.text: Public services should replace families in providing domestic work.
statements.agree: Housework and childcare should be provided as public services in place of being done within families.
statements.disagree: Public services should not replace families in providing domestic work.
statements.note: Domestic work means housework and childcare. About replacing family provision, not only offering public childcare alongside it.

statements.text: Words borrowed from foreign languages should be purged from the national language.
statements.agree: Foreign loanwords should be removed from the national language and replaced with native words.
statements.disagree: Words borrowed from foreign languages should not be purged from the national language.
statements.note: About removing foreign loanwords from the national language and replacing them with native words. Merely preferring native words is not enough.

statements.text: Changing a government's treaty with a nation within its borders should require that nation's consent.
statements.agree: A government must obtain the resident nation's agreement before rewriting or ending their treaty.
statements.disagree: A government should sometimes be entitled to rewrite or end such a treaty without the resident nation's consent.
statements.note: This concerns existing treaties with peoples within a state, including Indigenous nations. Changing includes cancellation; it does not require recognition of every claimed treaty or forbid a change agreed by both parties.

statements.text: Society should be reorganised into small self-governing cooperative communities that hold their property in common.
statements.agree: People should live and work in communities that own land and goods together and govern themselves.
statements.disagree: Society should not be reorganised into small self-governing cooperative communities that hold their property in common.
statements.note: About reorganising society into small self-governing communities that own their property in common. Having some cooperatives alongside other kinds of firms is not enough.

statements.text: The majority ethnic group should be encouraged to settle in regions where minorities are the majority.
statements.agree: The state should encourage the majority group to settle in regions where minorities are the majority.
statements.disagree: The majority ethnic group should not be encouraged to settle in regions where minorities are the majority.
statements.note: About the state encouraging members of the majority group to move to regions where minorities are the majority. People moving there on their own is not the same.

statements.text: Neither capitalism nor communism offers a sound basis for society.
statements.agree: Society should follow a third course beyond capitalism and communism.
statements.disagree: Society does not need a third course beyond capitalism and communism.
statements.note: Communism here refers to the system of collective economic ownership practiced in communist states. A regulated capitalist economy alone does not constitute a third system.

statements.text: A people's historical tie to a land gives it a stronger claim than other peoples living there now.
statements.agree: An ancestral bond to a land gives a people a claim that outweighs the claims of other peoples who now live there.
statements.disagree: A people's historical tie to a land does not give it a stronger claim than other peoples living there now.
statements.note: About ranking historical ties above current inhabitants' claims, not merely recognising historical connections.

statements.text: The Holocaust did not happen as historians describe it.
statements.agree: The mass murder of Europe's Jews by Nazi Germany was invented or greatly exaggerated.
statements.disagree: The Holocaust happened as historians describe it.
statements.note: About whether the Nazi mass murder of Europe's Jews happened as historians describe it. How it should be remembered is a different question.

statements.text: Sexual relations between adults of the same sex should be a criminal offence.
statements.agree: Same-sex relations between consenting adults should be punishable by law.
statements.disagree: The law should not punish consenting adults for same-sex relations.
statements.note: About criminal penalties for same-sex relations between consenting adults. Disapproving of them without making them a crime is not enough.

statements.text: Political opposition should be suppressed.
statements.agree: The government should stop its political opponents from organising, speaking or competing for power.
statements.disagree: Political opposition should not be suppressed.
statements.note: About political opposition, whatever the reason given for suppressing it. Banning parties that seek to abolish the constitutional order is a separate statement (ban-extremist-parties).

statements.text: Public blasphemy should be a crime.
statements.agree: The state should punish people who publicly insult what a religion holds sacred.
statements.disagree: Public blasphemy should not be a crime.
statements.note: About legal penalties for insulting religion. Punishing the practice of other religions is a separate question.

statements.text: A country's overseas territories should be governed for the economic benefit of the ruling country.
statements.agree: Colonies should be run mainly to supply markets, materials and outlets for the ruling country.
statements.disagree: A country's overseas territories should not be governed for the economic benefit of the ruling country.
statements.note: About whether overseas territories should be run mainly for the economic benefit of the ruling country. The territory also gaining from the arrangement doesn't count against it.

statements.text: Armed resistance to a non-Muslim invasion of Muslim land is a duty of every Muslim.
statements.agree: Every Muslim is obliged to take part in armed resistance against such an invasion.
statements.disagree: Armed resistance to a non-Muslim invasion of Muslim land is not a duty binding every Muslim.
statements.note: About whether every Muslim has a personal duty to join armed resistance when non-Muslim forces invade Muslim land. Believing such resistance is permitted is not enough.

statements.text: Failure to govern under religious law justifies armed overthrow of a ruler.
statements.agree: A ruler's failure to apply religious law is a sufficient ground for overthrowing that ruler with armed force.
statements.disagree: Failure to govern under religious law does not justify armed overthrow of a ruler.
statements.note: About religious-law noncompliance as a justification for armed overthrow. This does not require violence against every such ruler, specify a religion, or deny resistance on other grounds.

statements.text: Ordinary people should take part directly in the decisions that shape their daily lives.
statements.agree: People should have a direct role in making decisions where they work, live and study, rather than having those decisions made entirely for them.
statements.disagree: Ordinary people should not take part directly in the decisions that shape their daily lives.
statements.note: About an active role in decisions within everyday institutions, such as workplaces, neighbourhoods and universities. Participation means a real role in making decisions, not simply being informed of them. It does not require abolishing every representative, manager or official. Voting directly on national laws is asked separately.

statements.text: Overlapping forms of oppression must be addressed together.
statements.agree: Tackling oppression requires a combined approach to its overlapping forms, such as racism, sexism and class oppression.
statements.disagree: Overlapping forms of oppression should not be addressed together.
statements.note: About tackling racism, sexism, class oppression and similar forms of oppression together rather than one at a time. Opposing each of them separately is not enough.

statements.text: The law should recognise transgender people according to their gender identity.
statements.agree: Transgender people's legal gender should match their gender identity.
statements.disagree: The law should not recognise transgender people according to their gender identity.
statements.note: About legal recognition of gender identity, without specifying a recognition procedure or rules for every sex-separated activity.

statements.text: Medical professionals should be allowed to help terminally ill adults end their lives.
statements.agree: Terminally ill adults should be able to get medical help to die.
statements.disagree: Medical professionals should not be allowed to help terminally ill adults end their lives.
statements.note: About allowing medical professionals to help terminally ill adults end their lives, for example by providing a lethal drug. Withdrawing treatment or palliative care is a different question.

statements.text: The left-right division in politics is outdated.
statements.agree: Dividing politics into left and right no longer makes sense.
statements.disagree: The left-right division in politics remains meaningful.
statements.note: About whether those categories remain useful, without requiring a blend of their ideas.

statements.text: Work under capitalism alienates people from their own creative activity.
statements.agree: Wage work cuts people off from the meaning and creativity of what they make.
statements.disagree: Work under capitalism does not alienate people from their own creative activity.
statements.note: About whether working for wages, on tasks set by others, cuts people off from their own creativity.

statements.text: Islam is incompatible with Western values.
statements.agree: Islam fundamentally conflicts with the values of Western societies.
statements.disagree: Islam is compatible with Western values.
statements.note: About Islam as a religion, not simply extremist movements; incompatibility does not imply which side is preferable.

statements.text: Political authority ultimately comes from God.
statements.agree: God is the ultimate source of the right to exercise political authority.
statements.disagree: Political authority does not ultimately come from God.
statements.note: About the ultimate source of political authority, including views that it comes from God through the people. Belief in God alone does not imply agreement.

statements.text: Religious dress should be banned in state institutions.
statements.agree: State institutions stay free of visible religious dress for staff and pupils.
statements.disagree: Religious dress should not be banned in state institutions.
statements.note: About a ban on visible religious dress for officials, teachers and pupils in state institutions. Religious dress in private life is a different question.

statements.text: Employment contracts should never keep sexual harassment complaints out of court.
statements.agree: Employers should not be able to use nondisclosure agreements or mandatory arbitration to keep sexual harassment complaints out of court.
statements.disagree: Employment contracts should sometimes be able to keep sexual harassment complaints out of court.
statements.note: About limits on private contracts, such as nondisclosure agreements or arbitration clauses, that silence harassment claims.

statements.text: The economy should be a market economy with a public safety net.
statements.agree: Private businesses and markets should run most of the economy, while the government supports people who cannot meet their basic needs.
statements.disagree: The economy should not be a market economy with a public safety net.
statements.note: About the overall economic model. Disagreement can come from either side: rejecting a market economy, or rejecting public support within one. Competition rules are a separate statement (ban-cartels).

statements.text: Countries should abolish their armed forces.
statements.agree: A country can and should do without a standing military.
statements.disagree: Countries should keep their armed forces.
