statements.note: About doing without a standing military altogether. Cutting military spending or keeping only a small force is a different position.

statements.text: National development policy should allow some regions to become wealthy before others.
statements.agree: It is acceptable for a national development strategy to let some regions attain wealth before the rest.
statements.disagree: National development policy should not allow some regions to become wealthy before others.
statements.note: About accepting different regional development sequences as policy, not giving favoured individuals special privileges or claiming benefits automatically reach poorer regions.

statements.text: My country should stay out of the military blocs of rival great powers.
statements.agree: A country stays neutral and non-aligned rather than joining either bloc.
statements.disagree: My country should not stay out of the military blocs of rival great powers.
statements.note: About staying out of the military alliances led by rival great powers. Trading or having friendly relations with them is a different question.

statements.text: It is acceptable for a state's ruler to pass power to their child.
statements.agree: Someone who actually governs a state may hand that power on to their own child, whether as a king or as a republic's leader.
statements.disagree: It is not acceptable for a state's ruler to pass power to their child.
statements.note: About real governing power passing within a family. A ceremonial monarch who reigns without governing is a separate statement.

statements.text: User-owned banks lending at cost should replace profit-making banks.
statements.agree: Credit should come from banks owned by their users, charging only the costs of running the service, in place of profit-making banks.
statements.disagree: User-owned banks lending at cost should not replace profit-making banks.
statements.note: This concerns replacing profit-making credit provision with user-owned, cost-priced lending. It does not mean merely permitting credit unions, placing banks under state ownership or making every loan free of administrative costs. "At cost" excludes a profit margin; any treatment of lending risk needs source-specific clarification.

statements.text: Governments should refuse austerity conditions imposed by international lenders such as the IMF.
statements.agree: A country should reject spending cuts demanded in return for loans and set its own course.
statements.disagree: Governments should not refuse austerity conditions imposed by international lenders such as the IMF.
statements.note: About refusing the spending cuts that lenders such as the IMF attach to loans. Disliking a particular cut while accepting such conditions is not enough.

statements.text: The right to vote should be reserved for property owners.
statements.agree: Only people who own property should have the right to vote.
statements.disagree: People without property should also have the right to vote.
statements.note: About ownership as a condition for voting. This does not require a particular minimum property value or impose a tax-payment qualification.

statements.text: The domination of women is linked to the domination of nature.
statements.agree: The subordination of women is connected to human domination of the natural world.
statements.disagree: The domination of women is not linked to the domination of nature.
statements.note: About a connection between forms of domination, without separately prescribing a joint political strategy.

statements.text: Under capitalism, economic relationships between people appear as relationships between traded goods.
statements.agree: Capitalist exchange makes people's economic relationships look like relationships among the goods they trade.
statements.disagree: Under capitalism, economic relationships between people do not appear as relationships between traded goods.
statements.note: About the appearance of human economic relationships as relationships between commodities, not every kind of alienation, materialism or an assertion that economic forces literally have minds.

statements.text: Media owned by the rich make press freedom meaningless.
statements.agree: Formal press freedom is hollow when wealth decides who can actually be heard.
statements.disagree: Media owned by the rich do not make press freedom meaningless.
statements.note: About whether press freedom means little when wealthy owners control the media. Wanting rules on media ownership is a different question.

statements.text: Rulers should govern only under established public laws applied by recognised judges.
statements.agree: Rulers must act under lasting, publicly known laws administered by recognised courts.
statements.disagree: Rulers need not govern only under established public laws applied by recognised judges.
statements.note: About rulers being bound to lasting, published laws applied by recognised judges. Rulers making rules as they go is not the same.

statements.text: Only members of one ethnic group should be allowed to vote.
statements.agree: Only members of one racial or ethnic group should have the right to vote.
statements.disagree: Voting should not be limited to members of one ethnic group.
statements.note: Ethnic group here includes what is often called race. Eligibility for public office is a separate question.

statements.text: Citizens should have the option to vote online in public elections.
statements.agree: Eligible citizens should be entitled to cast their election ballots over the internet.
statements.disagree: Citizens should have no option to cast election ballots over the internet.
statements.note: This concerns an internet ballot option in public elections, not mandatory online voting, online debate, party consultations or private-platform polls. It does not change who is eligible to vote.

statements.text: Governments should publish records explaining their decisions.
statements.agree: The public should receive official records showing how government decisions were reached.
statements.disagree: Governments should sometimes withhold the records explaining their decisions.
statements.note: This concerns disclosure of decision records, not merely statistics, spending totals, citizen submissions or general promises of transparency. The statement states a broad publication duty; the disagree side includes exceptions.

statements.text: The law should restrict marriage between members of different religions.
statements.agree: The law may limit or closely check marriages between people of different religions.
statements.disagree: Adults may marry across religions without legal restriction.
statements.note: About laws limiting or closely checking marriage between people of different religions. A religion's own rules on whom its members may marry are a different question.

statements.text: Consumers should deliberately avoid shops owned by members of a particular religious minority.
statements.agree: People should deliberately avoid buying from shops owned by members of a particular religious minority.
statements.disagree: Consumers should not deliberately avoid shops owned by members of a particular religious minority.
statements.note: About deliberately avoiding shops because their owners belong to a particular religious minority. Avoiding a shop for other reasons is not the same.

statements.text: Randomly selected citizens' assemblies should help decide major public questions.
statements.agree: Groups of citizens chosen at random should meet to consider major public issues, with their conclusions contributing to policy decisions.
statements.disagree: Randomly selected citizens' assemblies should not help decide major public questions.
statements.note: A citizens' assembly here is a group chosen at random to consider public issues. "Help decide" means its conclusions have a role in public decisions; it does not require binding power, replacement of elected representatives or merely inviting anyone who volunteers to a meeting.

statements.text: Religious doctrine should be reinterpreted for modern conditions.
statements.agree: Inherited religious teachings should be understood anew in light of present conditions.
statements.disagree: Religious doctrine should not be reinterpreted for modern conditions.
statements.note: About interpreting religious teachings for present conditions, not necessarily changing religious law, abandoning faith, imposing state control or affirming every proposed reform.

statements.text: Great concentrations of wealth endanger a free society.
statements.agree: Very large concentrations of wealth threaten a free society.
statements.disagree: Great concentrations of wealth do not endanger a free society.
statements.note: About whether very large concentrations of wealth threaten a free society. Disliking inequality on other grounds is a different question.

statements.text: Gay people should be allowed to serve openly in the armed forces.
statements.agree: Gay people, including gay men and lesbians, should be permitted to serve without concealing their sexual orientation.
statements.disagree: Gay people should not be allowed to serve openly in the armed forces.
statements.note: "Gay people" includes lesbians. Open service means being open about sexual orientation, not an exemption from ordinary service rules. This does not ask about gender identity, compulsory service or whether armed forces should exist.

statements.text: State education should actively promote atheism.
statements.agree: Education provided by the state should encourage people to reject belief in God.
statements.disagree: State education should not actively promote atheism.
statements.note: About state education advocating atheism. Religious neutrality, teaching about atheism, freedom to criticise religion and compulsory unbelief are different positions.

statements.text: The police should be abolished.
statements.agree: Police forces should be abolished and replaced with other ways of keeping people safe.
statements.disagree: The police should not be abolished.
statements.note: About ending policing as an institution, not reforming, defunding or retraining it. Abolishing prisons is a separate question.

statements.text: In deeply divided societies, every major community should have a guaranteed share of executive power.
statements.agree: Each main community should have a guaranteed place in government, even against a numerical majority.
statements.disagree: Deeply divided societies should not guarantee every major community a share of executive power.
statements.note: About guaranteed participation of major communities in the executive, not merely minority rights, parliamentary seats, local autonomy or ordinary coalition politics.

statements.text: Private charity helps the poor better than government programs do.
statements.agree: Voluntary charitable help does a better job of helping people in poverty than government aid does.
statements.disagree: Private charity does not help people in poverty better than government programs do.
statements.note: A comparison of effectiveness, not whether charity is morally admirable or whether all government aid should be abolished. Community help counts here when it is voluntary charitable assistance, not merely local government provision.

statements.text: Elected politicians should be limited to a small number of terms in any office.
statements.agree: Elected politicians should serve only a small number of terms.
statements.disagree: Elected politicians should be able to serve any number of terms in any office.
statements.note: About capping how many terms one person can serve in elected office. Limiting the length of a single term is not enough.

statements.text: Citizens should have the right to delegate their votes separately for each policy area.
statements.agree: A citizen should be permitted to choose someone else to cast that citizen's votes in a policy area, with separate choices for different areas.
statements.disagree: Citizens should not have the right to delegate their votes separately for each policy area.
statements.note: This asks about personally transferring the exercise of policy votes, not electing a representative to an office, sending an assembly's mandated delegate or recalling an official. It leaves the duration and revocation rules open and does not require using the option.

statements.text: Reducing the risk of human extinction should be a top priority of public policy.
statements.agree: Preventing catastrophes that could end humanity deserves major, well-funded attention.
statements.disagree: Reducing the risk of human extinction should not be a top priority of public policy.
statements.note: About whether preventing human extinction, for example from pandemics or nuclear war, should rank among government's top priorities. Caring about it without making it a top priority is not enough.

statements.text: Women should be eligible for every religious leadership office on the same terms as men.
statements.agree: Every religious leadership role open to men should be open to women under the same eligibility rules.
statements.disagree: At least some religious leadership offices should have different eligibility rules for women than for men.
statements.note: About equal eligibility for religious leadership, not equal numbers of officeholders, religious teaching generally or state compulsion of religious bodies.

statements.text: Spouses should have equal authority within their marriage.
statements.agree: Spouses should make marital decisions as equals.
statements.disagree: Spouses should not have equal authority within their marriage.
statements.note: About equal decision-making authority between spouses, not identical household tasks or any prescribed gender combination.

statements.text: Foreign residents should be allowed to vote in local elections.
statements.agree: Long-term residents without citizenship have a say in the places where they live.
statements.disagree: Voting in local elections should be reserved for citizens.
statements.note: About letting non-citizens who live in a place vote in its local elections. Voting in national elections is a different question.

statements.text: Rents should be capped by law in areas of housing shortage.
statements.agree: The law limits how much landlords can charge where homes are scarce.
statements.disagree: Rents should be left uncapped by law in areas of housing shortage.
statements.note: About legal limits on rents where homes are scarce. Other housing policies, such as building more homes, are different questions.

statements.text: Intellectual property should be abolished.
statements.agree: Ideas and creative works can be copied freely; no one holds a legal monopoly on them.
statements.disagree: Intellectual property should not be abolished.
statements.note: About ending patents, copyrights and similar legal rights over ideas and creative works. Shorter or weaker protection is not enough.

statements.text: Young people should be organised into uniformed, drilled youth movements that train them for national service.
statements.agree: Youth belong to disciplined organisations that prepare them to serve the nation.
statements.disagree: Young people should not be organised into uniformed, drilled youth movements that train them for national service.
statements.note: About drilled, uniformed youth organisations that prepare young people to serve the nation. Voluntary scouts or sports clubs are not the same.

statements.text: Nuclear weapons should not be based on my country's territory.
statements.agree: No nuclear weapons, ours or an ally's, should be stationed here.
statements.disagree: Nuclear weapons may be based on my country's territory.
statements.note: About allowing no nuclear weapons, whoever owns them, to be stationed on the country's land. Opposing nuclear weapons elsewhere is a different question.

statements.text: A country should not host foreign military bases on its territory.
statements.agree: Foreign armies should not be based on the country's territory.
statements.disagree: A country may host foreign military bases on its territory.
statements.note: About allowing no foreign military bases on the country's land. Joining alliances or holding joint exercises is not the same.

statements.text: Governments should formally recognise past mass killings of a people as genocide.
statements.agree: States should officially name and acknowledge such killings.
statements.disagree: Governments should not formally recognise past mass killings of a people as genocide.
statements.note: About governments officially naming past mass killings of a people as genocide, such as the killing of Armenians in 1915. Mourning or condemning them without that word is not enough.

statements.text: Income should reward useful work, not merely the ownership of property.
statements.agree: Income from useful work should be rewarded ahead of income from merely owning property.
statements.disagree: Income may reward the mere ownership of property.
statements.note: About income from simply owning things, such as rent, interest or dividends, compared with income from work.

statements.text: Killing another person is wrong, even in self-defence.
statements.agree: Taking a life is never justified, even to stop an attacker.
statements.disagree: Killing another person can be right in self-defence or in defence of others.
statements.note: About whether killing is wrong in every case, including to stop an attacker. Opposing war or the death penalty is a different question.

statements.text: A nation's identity runs in unbroken continuity from its ancient origins to the present.
statements.agree: Today's nation is the same people as its ancient and medieval forebears.
statements.disagree: A nation's identity does not run in unbroken continuity from its ancient origins to the present.
statements.note: About whether today's nation is continuously the same people as its ancient and medieval forebears. Sharing a history or culture is not enough.

statements.text: Sex is socially constructed.
statements.agree: The categories used to classify people by sex are products of society.
statements.disagree: Sex is not socially constructed.
statements.note: About the social construction of sex categories, not a denial that bodies have biological features. Gender's social construction is a separate statement.

statements.text: Feminist politics should avoid relying on a single fixed definition of 'women'.
statements.agree: Feminist politics should avoid treating one unchanging definition of women as its foundation.
statements.disagree: A single fixed definition of women is an acceptable foundation for feminist politics.
statements.note: About whether feminist politics should avoid resting on one fixed definition of who counts as a woman. Whether feminism should work for women at all is a different question.

statements.text: Those who die for the nation should be honoured as martyrs.
statements.agree: People who give their lives for the nation deserve to be remembered as martyrs, with reverence beyond ordinary thanks.
statements.disagree: Those who die for the nation should not be honoured as martyrs.
statements.note: About treating those who die for the nation as martyrs, beyond ordinary civic remembrance.

statements.text: Politics is fundamentally a spiritual struggle against evil.
statements.agree: At its core, politics is a struggle between spiritual good and evil.
statements.disagree: Politics is not fundamentally a spiritual struggle against evil.
statements.note: "Spiritual" concerns forces or purposes beyond ordinary material interests; a moral disagreement alone is insufficient.

statements.text: A national homeland should give greater priority to supporting diaspora culture than to gathering all its people.
statements.agree: The homeland should place its cultural role for people abroad above the aim of bringing the whole people to live there.
statements.disagree: Gathering all the people in the homeland should have at least as much priority as supporting diaspora culture.
statements.note: Diaspora means members of a people living outside its homeland. Culture here includes religious heritage; supporting a diaspora does not rule out voluntary return.

statements.text: Cultural renewal of a nation should come before building its state.
statements.agree: A nation should revive its culture first and build its state afterward.
statements.disagree: Cultural renewal of a nation should not come before building its state.
statements.note: About reviving a nation's culture first and building its state afterward. Working on both at once is not enough.

statements.text: God should not be described in exclusively male terms.
statements.agree: Religious language and imagery should include more than male terms for God.
statements.disagree: God may be described in exclusively male terms.
statements.note: About whether religious language should use more than male terms for God. Women's roles in religion are a different question.

statements.text: Religious texts should be judged according to whether they promote women's full humanity.
statements.agree: Whether a religious text supports women as full human persons should be a standard for judging that text.
statements.disagree: Whether a religious text promotes women's full humanity should not be a standard for judging that text.
statements.note: "Full humanity" concerns treating women as full persons with dignity and agency, rather than as lesser beings. The question is whether this is a standard for evaluating the text itself, not only later interpretations or religious customs. It does not prescribe state censorship or identify women as the only people entitled to interpret scripture.

statements.text: A country's national majority should control its economy.
statements.agree: The country's main national or ethnic group should have the leading role in controlling economic life.
statements.disagree: A country's national majority should not control its economy.
statements.note: About economic control based on national-group membership, rather than citizenship alone.

statements.text: Administrative regions where one people live should be merged into a single territorial unit for that people.
statements.agree: A people should have one region of its own rather than being split across several.
statements.disagree: Administrative regions where one people live should not be merged into a single territorial unit for that people.
statements.note: About merging regions where one people lives into a single territorial unit for that people. Giving a people cultural rights without changing borders is not enough.

statements.text: Trade unions should be independent of the state.
statements.agree: Trade unions should control their own affairs without state direction.
statements.disagree: Trade unions should not be independent of the state.
statements.note: About organisational autonomy from government, not exemption from ordinary law or voluntary affiliation with a political party.

statements.text: Socialism requires the working class itself to hold real political power.
statements.agree: Without workers' own political power, state ownership is not socialism.
statements.disagree: A society can be socialist without the working class itself holding political power.
statements.note: About whether state ownership counts as socialism when the working class itself holds no real political power. Whether socialism is desirable is a different question.

statements.text: Essential local services should be publicly owned.
statements.agree: Basic local services, such as water, hospitals and local transport, stay publicly owned and run.
statements.disagree: Essential local services should not be publicly owned.
statements.note: About keeping basic local services public. Ownership of major industries is a separate question.

statements.text: A legislature should include a second chamber alongside the directly elected parliament.
statements.agree: A legislature should have a second chamber as well as its directly elected parliament.
statements.disagree: A legislature should not include a second chamber alongside the directly elected parliament.
statements.note: About having a second chamber, such as a senate, alongside the directly elected parliament. How its members are chosen is a different question.

statements.text: The means of production should be owned by the local community, neither by private owners nor by the national state.
statements.agree: Farms, factories and utilities belong to the town or city that uses them.
statements.disagree: Local community ownership of the means of production should not replace private or state ownership.
statements.note: About local communities, such as towns and cities, owning farms, factories and utilities. Ownership by the national state or by private owners doesn't count.

statements.text: Local communities should form joint councils limited to carrying out decisions made in local assemblies.
statements.agree: Towns and cities should link through councils whose delegates coordinate and administer what local assemblies decide, without making policy themselves.
statements.disagree: Local communities should not form joint councils limited to carrying out decisions made in local assemblies.
statements.note: About a network of self-governing communities: local assemblies make policy; their joint councils implement it.

statements.text: A worker's wage should be enough to support their whole family.
statements.agree: One worker's pay should cover the living needs of that worker's family, including the worker.
statements.disagree: A worker's wage need not be enough to support their whole family.
statements.note: This is a wage-sufficiency standard for workers of any gender. It does not assign anyone a breadwinner role, require another family member to stay home, prescribe different pay for men and women or require pay to vary with the number of dependants. It asks about wages rather than total household income from benefits or several earners.

statements.text: Governments should fund research aimed at slowing biological ageing.
statements.agree: Public funding should support research intended to slow the biological ageing process.
statements.disagree: Governments should provide no funding for research aimed at slowing biological ageing.
statements.note: This concerns slowing ageing itself, not merely treating a particular disease common in old age. It does not specify an increase from current funding, reversing existing ageing or universal access to future treatments.

statements.text: People should have access to payments untraceable to the government.
statements.agree: People should be able to make payments whose participants the government cannot identify.
statements.disagree: The government should have the ability to identify the participants in every payment.
statements.note: This asks whether an untraceable payment option should exist, not whether every payment must be anonymous. It does not separately guarantee immunity from account freezes or payment blocking.

statements.text: People should have the right to participate online without disclosing their legal identities.
statements.agree: People should be entitled to take part online anonymously or under a pseudonym without mandatory disclosure of their legal identity.
statements.disagree: Online participation should sometimes require disclosure of a person's legal identity.
statements.note: This concerns compulsory identification, including disclosure to a platform or official registry, not merely whether a legal name appears publicly. A pseudonym linked to mandatory identity verification is different from this right.

statements.text: The state should serve each person without treating anyone merely as a tool for collective goals.
statements.agree: Government should serve people's good while respecting each person as more than an instrument of the state or community.
statements.disagree: Collective goals can justify treating a person merely as a tool.
statements.note: "Merely" matters: social duties and policies serving a common good are compatible with recognising each person's own worth. This is not a veto on every policy imposing individual costs.

statements.text: Politics should serve people's spiritual needs.
statements.agree: Politics should support people's spiritual well-being.
statements.disagree: Politics should not serve people's spiritual needs.
statements.note: About a purpose of politics, rather than a separate claim about the composition of human nature.

statements.text: The national legislature should be able to take back any powers it gives to regions.
statements.agree: The national parliament stays the final authority and can take powers back from the regions.
statements.disagree: The national legislature should not be able to take back powers given to regions on its own.
statements.note: About whether a region's powers can be taken back by the national parliament, as in the UK, or are protected, as in a federal constitution.

statements.text: Genetically engineered crops should be embraced as a tool for sustainable agriculture.
statements.agree: Genetically engineered crops are a good tool for sustainable agriculture.
statements.disagree: Genetically engineered crops should not be embraced as a tool for sustainable agriculture.
statements.note: About welcoming genetically engineered crops as a tool for sustainable agriculture. Using them in some cases without embracing them is not enough.

statements.text: Dense cities produce lower greenhouse-gas emissions per resident than suburbs.
statements.agree: Average emissions per person are lower in compact cities than in suburban settlements.
statements.disagree: Dense cities produce at least as much greenhouse-gas emissions per resident as suburbs.
statements.note: This compares per-person emissions, not total emissions, local air quality, land use or the moral value of city life. It makes no comparison with rural settlements.

statements.text: Each racial group should organise to defend its distinct political interests.
statements.agree: Members of every racial group should organise politically around interests specific to their group.
statements.disagree: Racial groups should not each organise to defend distinct political interests of their own.
statements.note: About race as a basis for political organisation. It does not require racial interests to be biological or every member of a group to agree.

statements.text: Pride in one's own race is legitimate.
statements.agree: It is legitimate to take pride in the racial group one belongs to.
statements.disagree: Pride in one's own race is not legitimate.
statements.note: About racial pride, not racial superiority, ancestry generally, citizenship, cultural achievement or national patriotism.

statements.text: Armed forces should be used only to defend the country against attack, never to start wars.
statements.agree: Force is for self-defence alone.
statements.disagree: Armed forces should not be used only to defend the country against attack, never to start wars.
statements.note: About whether armed forces may ever be used to start a war, rather than only to defend the country against attack. Having a strong army is not the same.

statements.text: A shared language is enough to make a people one nation.
statements.agree: Speaking a common language is sufficient for people to constitute one nation.
statements.disagree: Sharing a language is not sufficient for people to constitute one nation.
statements.note: About whether a common language is sufficient, not whether every nation must speak one language. It concerns national identity, not a right to one state.

statements.text: Members of each religious community should vote for their own representatives in separate electorates.
statements.agree: Each community should elect its own representatives.
statements.disagree: Members of each religious community should not vote for their own representatives in separate electorates.
statements.note: About separate voter rolls for each religious community, for example Muslims voting only for Muslim seats in British India. Reserved seats chosen by all voters are a different question.

statements.text: Preventing foreign-backed territorial partition should be a central aim of national policy.
statements.agree: National policy should give priority to preventing outside powers from splitting the country territorially.
statements.disagree: Preventing foreign-backed territorial partition need not be a central aim of national policy.
statements.note: About an alleged foreign plan to divide the country territorially. General hostility, economic pressure, internal social division or a plan to overthrow its government is insufficient.

statements.text: Public higher education should charge no tuition.
statements.agree: Students should pay no tuition to attend public higher education institutions.
statements.disagree: Public higher education should not be universally tuition-free.
statements.note: About tuition charges at public higher education institutions, not free admission regardless of qualifications, living expenses or cancellation of past student debt.

statements.text: Taxing polluters should do more to protect the environment than regulating them.
statements.agree: Taxing polluters should do more to protect the environment than regulating them.
statements.disagree: Regulating polluters should do at least as much to protect the environment as taxing them.
statements.note: About whether charging polluters does more for the environment than setting legal limits on what they may emit. Wanting both together doesn't say which does more.

statements.text: Present generations owe it to future generations to hand on the Earth undamaged.
statements.agree: We have a duty to leave the planet in good condition for those who come after us.
statements.disagree: Present generations do not owe it to future ones to hand on the Earth undamaged.
statements.note: About a duty to leave the Earth in good condition for later generations, for example its climate, soil and water. Caring about the environment for today's people is not the same.

statements.text: Women tend to be more compassionate than men.
statements.agree: Women, on average, show greater concern for others' suffering than men do.
statements.disagree: Women do not tend to be more compassionate than men.
statements.note: This compares a tendency, not every individual. It does not claim an innate cause, divide everyone into two genders or prescribe different political rights.

statements.text: Armaments should be kept at the minimum needed for national safety.
statements.agree: Countries should maintain only the weapons needed for national safety.
statements.disagree: Armaments need not be limited to the minimum needed for national safety.
statements.note: About the minimum defensible level of armaments, not a requirement for international agreement.

statements.text: International agreements between governments should never be secret.
statements.agree: Every treaty and agreement between governments should be made public.
statements.disagree: Governments should be able to keep some international agreements secret.
statements.note: About secret treaties and agreements. Keeping negotiations confidential until a public agreement is reached is a separate question.

statements.text: The state should control the movement of capital across its borders.
statements.agree: Governments should limit how money and investment can be moved across borders.
statements.disagree: The state should not control the movement of capital across its borders.
statements.note: About limits on moving money and investment into or out of a country. Controls on trade in goods are a different question.

statements.text: Only state forces should be allowed to bear arms.
statements.agree: Only the state's armed forces and police should have permission to carry weapons.
statements.disagree: People outside state forces should also be allowed to bear arms.
statements.note: About an exclusive state right to carry weapons, including the exclusion of private citizens, not merely a ban on private armies.

statements.text: Soldiers should refuse orders to fight in wars between states.
statements.agree: Individual soldiers and conscripts have a duty to refuse to fight in state wars.
statements.disagree: Soldiers should not refuse orders to fight in wars between states.
statements.note: About whether soldiers should refuse orders to fight in wars between states. Opposing a particular war as a citizen is not the same.

statements.text: Union negotiations with employers should set workers' wages.
statements.agree: Workers' pay should be settled in collective bargaining between their union and their employer.
statements.disagree: Workers' wages should not be set in union negotiations with employers.
statements.note: About collective wage setting as the preferred arrangement, not simply permission to join a union or the exclusive use of sector-wide contracts.

statements.text: Governments should top up the incomes of low-paid working families through tax credits.
statements.agree: The state adds to the pay of low-income working households through the tax system.
statements.disagree: Governments should not top up the incomes of low-paid working families through tax credits.
statements.note: About the state adding to the low earnings of working families through tax credits. A higher minimum wage, or benefits only for people without jobs, is not the same.

statements.text: The law should limit government borrowing.
statements.agree: Government borrowing should be subject to binding legal limits.
statements.disagree: Government borrowing should be free of binding legal limits.
statements.note: This concerns legal constraints on borrowing, including constitutional debt rules. It does not prescribe a balanced budget every year, ban all borrowing, exclude defined emergency exceptions or equate a political target with a legal rule. Limits on spending alone do not necessarily limit borrowing.

statements.text: The rules of the international economy should be restructured in favour of developing countries.
statements.agree: Trade, finance and debt rules should be changed to give poorer countries a fairer share.
statements.disagree: International economic rules should not be reshaped to favour developing countries.
statements.note: About changing the rules of trade, finance and debt to favour developing countries. Giving aid within the current rules is not enough.

statements.text: The state's governing institutions should be replaced with fundamentally different ones.
statements.agree: Political change should replace the existing administrative and coercive institutions with new forms of organization, rather than put new leaders in charge of the old apparatus.
statements.disagree: The existing governing institutions should be retained, even if their personnel, policies or procedures change.
statements.note: About replacing the state's institutional structure, such as its bureaucracy, armed forces, police and courts. Replacement could involve a new state or forms of organization without a state. This does not ask whether violence is justified, whether all public services should disappear, or whether a particular incumbent should lose office.

statements.text: Different communities should be free to try different economic systems, with no fixed blueprint for the economy of a free society.
statements.agree: Communities should be free to choose their own economic arrangements, and a free society has no fixed blueprint for its economy.
statements.disagree: Different communities should not be free to try different economic systems, with no fixed blueprint for the economy of a free society.
statements.note: About letting communities try different economic arrangements, with no single plan for how a free society's economy must work. One system imposed on every community is a different position.

statements.text: Ecosystems should be valued as capital in economic accounts.
statements.agree: Economic accounts should record ecosystems as assets whose depletion counts as a loss.
statements.disagree: Economic accounts should exclude ecosystems from capital valuation.
statements.note: An ecosystem is a functioning natural community. This concerns valuing that asset in accounts, not requiring private ownership, tradable credits or treating monetary value as its only worth.

statements.text: The nation is a sacred community that outlasts its members, giving their lives lasting meaning.
statements.agree: The nation is a sacred, enduring community in which individuals find lasting meaning.
statements.disagree: The nation is not a sacred community that outlasts its members, giving their lives lasting meaning.
statements.note: About seeing the nation as a sacred community that outlasts its members and gives their lives meaning. Ordinary patriotism or pride in one's country is not enough.

statements.text: Governments should cancel at least part of graduates' outstanding student loan debt.
statements.agree: Government action should write off some or all of the student loan balance that graduates already owe.
statements.disagree: Governments should not cancel any of graduates' outstanding student loan debt.
statements.note: This concerns writing off existing balances, not solely lowering future interest, extending repayment time, subsidising tuition or making new loans cheaper. It does not require complete cancellation, specify which graduates qualify or prescribe executive action without legislative authority.

statements.text: A country's richer regions owe their wealth to exploiting its poorer regions.
statements.agree: Within a country, the richer regions grew rich by draining the poorer ones, much as colonial powers drained their colonies.
statements.disagree: A country's richer regions do not owe their wealth to exploiting its poorer regions.
statements.note: About regions within one country, as in claims of internal colonialism. A claim that a rich region is drained by poorer ones is the opposite view.

statements.text: A shared human nature is the basis of human rights.
statements.agree: Human rights come from the nature that all human beings share.
statements.disagree: A shared human nature is not the basis of human rights.
statements.note: About human rights resting on the nature all people share, rather than on laws, agreements or a government's grant. Simply supporting human rights is not enough.

statements.text: Governments should fund public service media free from government editorial control.
statements.agree: Public service media should receive government funding without government officials deciding their editorial content.
statements.disagree: Governments should not fund public service media free from government editorial control.
statements.note: This asks for public funding with editorial independence from government. It does not require a ban on advertising, eliminate commercial influence, prescribe a licence fee or exempt outlets from ordinary legal and financial accountability.

statements.text: All authentic religions express one underlying spiritual truth.
statements.agree: Behind their different forms, the great religions point to one shared truth.
statements.disagree: Not all authentic religions express one underlying spiritual truth.
statements.note: About whether the great religions all point to one shared spiritual truth beneath their differences. Respecting other religions is not enough.

statements.text: The state should protect farmers from swings in market prices.
statements.agree: Farmers should get price floors, state buying or cheap credit to keep them secure.
statements.disagree: The state should not protect farmers from swings in market prices.
statements.note: About state protection for farmers against price swings, such as price floors, state buying or cheap credit. General help for rural areas is not the same.

statements.text: Countries facing nuclear-armed rivals should retain their nuclear weapons.
statements.agree: A country with nuclear weapons should keep them for as long as its rivals retain theirs.
statements.disagree: Countries facing nuclear-armed rivals should not retain their nuclear weapons.
statements.note: About rejecting complete unilateral nuclear disarmament in the presence of nuclear-armed rivals, not opposing negotiated disarmament, arsenal reductions or restrictions on use.

statements.text: Working people should have their own political party, independent of the established parties.
statements.agree: Workers need a party of their own to represent their interests in government.
statements.disagree: Working people should not have their own political party, independent of the established parties.
statements.note: About working people having a party of their own, independent of the established parties. Voting for an existing party that favours workers is not enough.

statements.text: Women should have the same legal rights to land as men.
statements.agree: Daughters and widows inherit and own land on the same terms as sons and husbands.
statements.disagree: Women should not have the same legal rights to land as men.
statements.note: About women having the same legal rights as men to own and inherit land, as daughters and widows. Equal rights in other areas of law are a different question.

statements.text: A language spoken in several regions is one language, whatever name each region gives it.
statements.agree: Varieties spoken across regions are one language, even if each region names it differently.
statements.disagree: A language spoken in several regions is not one language, whatever name each region gives it.
statements.note: About whether a language spoken in several regions counts as one language despite different local names, for example Serbian, Croatian and Bosnian. Whether those regions form one country is a different question.

statements.text: Compensation lawsuits for proven pollution damage to property should replace agency regulation.
statements.agree: Pollution should be dealt with through lawsuits compensating owners for proven physical damage to their property, in place of environmental-agency regulation.
statements.disagree: Compensation lawsuits for proven pollution damage to property should not replace agency regulation.
statements.note: This concerns replacing regulation with compensation claims for proven physical property damage. It does not merely add lawsuits alongside agencies, ask about court orders stopping pollution, prescribe private rather than public courts or cover every form of ecological harm.

statements.text: Customary chiefs should have an official advisory role in making national law.
statements.agree: Customary chiefs should have an official advisory role in making national law.
statements.disagree: Customary chiefs should not have an official advisory role in making national law.
statements.note: About a formal advisory role for traditional chiefs in making national law. Chiefs ruling local customary matters is a different question.

statements.text: Protecting the environment should take priority over individual liberty.
statements.agree: When people's freedom to do something harms the environment, the law should limit that freedom.
statements.disagree: When people's freedom to do something harms the environment, protecting the environment should not take priority over that freedom.
statements.note: About everyday freedoms, such as how people use their land, run their businesses, travel and what they buy, when these harm the environment.

statements.text: Serious repeat offenders should face mandatory minimum sentences.
statements.agree: The law should require a minimum sentence for serious repeat offenders, preventing judges from sentencing below that minimum.
statements.disagree: Serious repeat offenders should not necessarily face mandatory minimum sentences.
statements.note: A mandatory minimum is a legal floor, not a single fixed sentence. Judges might impose a longer term. This does not prescribe a particular number of years, apply to every first offence or equate heavier penalties with limits on judicial discretion.

statements.text: Immigrants should be required to learn the national language.
statements.agree: Learning the language is a duty of settling, and the state may require it.
statements.disagree: Immigrants should not be required to learn the national language.
statements.note: About requiring immigrants to learn the national language, for example as a condition of settling. Offering free classes, or merely hoping they learn it, is not enough.

statements.text: Paying a union should never be a condition of employment.
statements.agree: Workers should be entitled to take or keep a job without being required to pay a union, including representation fees charged to nonmembers.
statements.disagree: Payment to a union should be permitted as a condition of employment in at least some circumstances.
statements.note: This concerns compulsory payments linked to a job, not formal union membership, voluntary contributions, collective-bargaining rights or whether unions are beneficial. State-imposed dues and union-security clauses in employment contracts may have different justifications, which sources must address.

statements.text: Voters should have to present photographic identification at polling stations.
statements.agree: People voting in person should be required to show photo ID.
statements.disagree: People should have the right to vote in person without presenting photo ID.
statements.note: Photo identification verifies identity; it need not prove citizenship. This concerns casting an in-person ballot, not documentary eligibility checks during registration or identification numbers on postal ballots.

statements.text: No single interpretation of a religion should have legal precedence over others in the state.
statements.agree: The state should treat all streams and interpretations of a religion equally under the law.
statements.disagree: A single interpretation of a religion may have legal precedence over others in the state.
statements.note: About whether the state may favour one branch or reading of a religion in law, for example one Christian church or one school of Islam.

statements.text: Fair elections are all a government needs to be democratic, whatever policies it pursues.
statements.agree: Democracy is a method for choosing and removing rulers, and fair elections are enough to make a government democratic.
statements.disagree: A government needs more than fair elections to be democratic.
statements.note: About whether fair elections alone make a government democratic, whatever it does with its power. Valuing elections is not enough.

statements.text: Sex outside marriage is acceptable for women.
statements.agree: A woman who has sex outside marriage is not doing anything wrong.
statements.disagree: Sex outside marriage is not acceptable for women.
statements.note: About consenting adults, including sex before marriage, and whether marriage is a moral requirement for women. Legal freedom is a separate question.

statements.text: Governments should have the right to shut down internet access to maintain public order.
statements.agree: A government should sometimes be entitled to stop internet connectivity across an area for public-order reasons.
statements.disagree: Governments should have no right to shut down internet access for public-order reasons.
statements.note: Shutdown means stopping general internet connectivity for an area, not merely blocking a website, filtering content or responding to a technical outage.

statements.text: Welfare programs should be replaced by a cash payment that shrinks as a person's earnings rise.
statements.agree: One cash payment, withdrawn gradually as income grows, should replace separate welfare programs.
statements.disagree: Welfare programs should not be replaced by a cash payment that shrinks as earnings rise.
statements.note: About replacing separate welfare programs with one cash payment that shrinks gradually as earnings rise. A payment given to everyone, or one added on top of existing programs, is not the same.

statements.text: Women should have the same political rights as men.
statements.agree: Women vote and stand for office on the same terms as men.
statements.disagree: Women should not have the same political rights as men.
statements.note: About women's political rights, such as voting and holding public office. Equality at work or in family law is a different question.

statements.text: Religion is a major cause of women's oppression.
statements.agree: Religious teaching and institutions are a main reason women have been held down.
statements.disagree: Religion is not a major cause of women's oppression.
statements.note: About whether religious teaching and institutions are a main reason women have been held down. Religion having some effect on women's status is not enough.

statements.text: Racial categories are social constructs without a scientific basis.
statements.agree: Races are not natural scientific divisions of humanity but categories created by society.
statements.disagree: Racial categories are not merely social constructs without a scientific basis.
statements.note: About whether races are natural divisions of humanity or categories created by society. Whether racism and its effects are real is a different question.

statements.text: Governments should have dedicated agencies to promote gender equality.
statements.agree: Government bodies should be specifically responsible for advancing gender equality.
statements.disagree: Governments should not have dedicated agencies to promote gender equality.
statements.note: About dedicated government institutions for gender equality. No particular institutional form, level of government or equality policy is required. General support for equality alone does not establish support for such agencies.

statements.text: Land belongs to whoever first puts it to use.
statements.agree: Whoever first settles and works unowned land becomes its rightful owner.
statements.disagree: Land does not belong to whoever first puts it to use.
statements.note: About land that no one owns becoming the property of whoever first settles and works it. Buying land or inheriting it is a different question.

statements.text: Political leaders responsible for atrocities should face trial in international criminal courts.
statements.agree: International criminal courts should try political leaders responsible for atrocities such as genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes.
statements.disagree: International criminal trials should not be required for every political leader responsible for atrocities.
statements.note: This concerns individual criminal responsibility for atrocities, not lawsuits against states, the separate crime of aggression or a requirement to use the permanent ICC rather than an international tribunal established for a particular conflict. Trials require due process; an allegation alone does not establish guilt.

statements.text: Scripture is God's error-free word.
statements.agree: Religious scripture is God's word without any error.
statements.disagree: Scripture is not God's error-free word.
statements.note: About the divine inerrancy of the scripture a person regards as sacred. This does not require a literal interpretation of every passage or assume all religions recognise the same texts.

statements.text: New Indigenous self-government arrangements should guarantee women's equal participation.
statements.agree: Women should have an equal right to participate in Indigenous self-government from its establishment.
statements.disagree: New Indigenous self-government arrangements should sometimes be permitted without a guarantee of women's equal participation.
statements.note: Equal participation means equal rights to take part in governing, not a fixed numerical quota. This selects Indigenous self-government; broader national autonomy and equality in other areas require separate evidence.

statements.text: A state with a state-owned planned economy should be defended against capitalist restoration despite its ruling bureaucracy.
statements.agree: A state whose economy is publicly owned and planned should be defended against a return to capitalism even if a bureaucracy rules it.
statements.disagree: A state with a state-owned planned economy should not be defended against capitalist restoration under a ruling bureaucracy.
statements.note: About defending the economic system despite bureaucratic rulers, without endorsing those rulers.

statements.text: Council delegates should choose officials for higher levels of government.
statements.agree: Delegates selected by councils at one level should select officeholders at higher levels.
statements.disagree: Council delegates should not choose officials for higher levels of government.
statements.note: About selection upward from councils, not every indirect election, appointment from above, direct decisions on local policy or a restriction on the franchise.

statements.text: A country's traditional national church should have a special legal status above other religious bodies.
statements.agree: The national church is recognised in law above other religions.
statements.disagree: A country's traditional national church should not have a special legal status above other religious bodies.
statements.note: About giving a country's traditional church a special legal rank above other religious bodies. Simply being its largest or oldest church is not enough.

statements.text: Regions where an ethnic minority forms the majority should have territorial autonomy within the state.
statements.agree: Such regions should run many of their own affairs.
statements.disagree: Regions where an ethnic minority forms the majority should not have territorial autonomy within the state.
statements.note: About self-government for regions where an ethnic minority is the local majority, within the existing state. Full independence is a different question.

statements.text: The inhabitants of a disputed territory should decide by vote which country it belongs to.
statements.agree: The people who live there should choose.
statements.disagree: The inhabitants of a disputed territory should not decide by vote which country it belongs to.
statements.note: About letting the people living in a disputed territory vote on which country it belongs to. Deciding by treaty, history or military control is not the same.

statements.text: A newly independent state should retain its inherited colonial borders.
statements.agree: The state should keep the colonial-era boundaries it inherits at independence.
statements.disagree: A newly independent state should sometimes redraw its inherited colonial borders.
statements.note: This concerns the territorial boundaries inherited at independence, not endorsement of colonial rule or a ban on cooperation between states.

statements.text: People should keep their material wants to a minimum.
statements.agree: People should want as few material things as possible.
statements.disagree: People should not keep their material wants to a minimum.
statements.note: About limited material wants as a personal ideal, not economic isolation, compulsory poverty or a prohibition on trade.

statements.text: The authorities should restrict outside settlement in regions where an indigenous people is the original majority.
statements.agree: Settlement by outsiders should be limited to protect the indigenous majority.
statements.disagree: The authorities should not restrict outside settlement in regions where an indigenous people is the original majority.
statements.note: About authorities limiting outsiders moving into regions where an indigenous people is the original majority. Protecting indigenous land ownership alone is not enough.

statements.text: Women should have the same military draft obligations as men.
statements.agree: Women and men should face identical draft obligations, including no obligations for either group when the draft is abolished.
statements.disagree: Women should have different military draft obligations from men.
statements.note: Draft obligations include registration and compulsory military service. Equal obligations do not require identical military assignments. This compares women with men without classifying everyone into two genders.

statements.text: A nation has a spiritual bond with its ancestral homeland.
statements.agree: A people's connection to its ancestral land is spiritual, beyond practical interests or ordinary affection.
statements.disagree: A nation has no spiritual bond with its ancestral homeland.
statements.note: "Nation" means a people, not necessarily an existing state. "Spiritual" is stronger than a historical connection or a territorial claim. A duty to defend the land is a separate matter.

statements.text: States should have the right to execute suspected drug dealers without trial.
statements.agree: A state should be entitled to put suspected drug dealers to death without trying them first.
statements.disagree: States should have no right to execute suspected drug dealers without trial.
statements.note: Execute means kill as punishment. This does not ask about necessary defence against an immediate attack, or assume that an allegation establishes guilt. Drug users are outside this narrower question.

statements.text: A country should seek closer ties with China than with the United States.
statements.agree: A country should seek closer ties with China than with the United States.
statements.disagree: A country should seek ties with the United States at least as close as its ties with China.
statements.note: About a country seeking closer ties with China than with the United States, in trade, diplomacy or security. Good relations with both is not enough.

statements.text: A state should look after members of its nation living as minorities in neighbouring countries.
statements.agree: A state should take responsibility for the welfare of its national communities across neighbouring borders.
statements.disagree: A state should not look after members of its nation living as minorities in neighbouring countries.
statements.note: About a state's responsibility toward its national communities in neighbouring countries. The claim specifies no particular aid programme, annexation policy or permission to use force.

statements.text: Whoever takes natural resources for their own use owes compensation to everyone else.
statements.agree: Whoever uses land or resources owes the rest of society a share of their value.
statements.disagree: Whoever takes natural resources for their own use does not owe compensation to everyone else.
statements.note: About whether those who take natural resources such as land owe the rest of society a share of their value. Taxing income or wealth in general is not the same.

statements.text: Each person has full ownership of their own body.
statements.agree: A person's body belongs entirely to that person.
statements.disagree: People do not have full ownership of their own bodies.
statements.note: About ownership of one's body, rather than ownership of income or the products of work.

statements.text: Basic necessities should be exempt from consumption taxes.
statements.agree: Purchases of basic necessities should carry no consumption tax.
statements.disagree: At least some basic necessities should be subject to consumption taxes.
statements.note: Consumption taxes include retail sales tax, VAT and excise duties on purchases. This concerns necessities, not luxuries or taxes on income.

statements.text: Social programmes limited to the poorest should replace universal social programmes.
statements.agree: Universal social programmes should give way to programmes restricted to the poorest people, with eligibility based on financial need.
statements.disagree: Social programmes limited to the poorest should not replace universal social programmes.
statements.note: This concerns replacing universal provision with poverty-based eligibility, not merely adding extra help for disadvantaged people. It does not equate nationality, age, disability, work requirements or contributions with an income test. It asks about the general design of social provision, not one isolated benefit.

statements.text: The leader should deal directly with the people without political intermediaries.
statements.agree: The leader should bypass parties and organised interest groups in dealing with the people.
statements.disagree: The leader should not bypass political intermediaries in dealing with the people.
statements.note: Political intermediaries means organised bodies representing people to their leader, not advisers or administrative staff.

statements.text: Governments should not give special legal privileges to well-connected businesses.
statements.agree: No subsidies, licences or protections that favour firms close to government.
statements.disagree: Governments may give special legal privileges to well-connected businesses.
statements.note: About governments not giving subsidies, licences or protections to firms close to them. Ordinary rules that apply to every business alike don't count against it.

statements.text: Politics should not be organised along religious denominations.
statements.agree: Parties and offices should cut across religious lines.
statements.disagree: Politics may be organised along religious denominations.
statements.note: About religion as a basis for organising politics, for example Lebanon, where top offices are shared out between religious communities. Religious people taking part in politics is a different question.

statements.text: Modern technology should be combined with a revival of ancestral values.
statements.agree: Society should use modern technology together with revived values inherited from its ancestors.
statements.disagree: Modern technology should not be combined with a revival of ancestral values.
statements.note: This concerns the proposed combination of technology with revived inherited values. It does not endorse every old custom, unlimited technological development, a particular religion or the distinct political programme called archeofuturism. Preserving heritage objects or language alone does not establish the value-revival claim.

statements.text: Women should be able to initiate divorce without their husband's consent.
statements.agree: A wife can end the marriage even when her husband refuses.
statements.disagree: Women should not be able to initiate divorce without their husband's consent.
statements.note: About whether a wife can divorce against her husband's will.

statements.text: Countries should control their own natural resources.
statements.agree: Each country should hold ultimate authority over its natural resources, without foreign interests controlling them.
statements.disagree: Countries should not necessarily control their own natural resources.
statements.note: National control does not necessarily mean state ownership of every enterprise or a ban on foreign investment. The issue is who holds final authority over resources within a country. It does not give a country a right to control another country's resources or guarantee domestic self-sufficiency.

statements.text: Whether a distribution of wealth is just depends on how it came about, not on how equal it is.
statements.agree: Whether a distribution of wealth is fair depends on how it came about, not on how equal it is.
statements.disagree: Whether a distribution of wealth is just does not depend only on how it came about.
statements.note: About whether a distribution of wealth is fair because of how people came by it, not because of how equal the result is. Thinking some inequality is acceptable is not enough.

statements.text: A small tax should be charged on international financial transactions such as currency trades.
statements.agree: A small tax should be charged on international financial transactions such as currency trades.
statements.disagree: A small tax should not be charged on international financial transactions such as currency trades.
statements.note: About a small tax on financial trading across borders, such as buying and selling currencies (a "Tobin tax").

statements.text: Racism is no longer the main obstacle to the advancement of disadvantaged racial groups.
statements.agree: Other factors such as policy, family and culture now hold people back more than racism does.
statements.disagree: Racism is still the main obstacle to the advancement of disadvantaged racial groups.
statements.note: About whether racism is still the main thing holding back disadvantaged racial groups today. Racism being serious in the past is a different question.

statements.text: Unjust laws carry no moral obligation of obedience.
statements.agree: A law imposes no moral duty to obey it if the law is unjust.
statements.disagree: At least some unjust laws impose a moral duty of obedience.
statements.note: This concerns moral obligation, not whether a rule legally counts as law, whether courts will enforce it or whether disobedience is prudent. It does not assert a duty to disobey, permission for violence or immunity from legal penalties.

statements.text: Society should use automation to minimise people's necessary working hours.
statements.agree: Automation should be directed towards making the time people need to spend working as short as feasible.
statements.disagree: Society should not aim to minimise necessary working hours using automation.
statements.note: Necessary work is work needed to meet people's material needs. Voluntary creative activity need not disappear. This asks the social aim of automation, not a prediction that machines will achieve it or a particular income-distribution scheme.

statements.text: The world should have several independent centres of power.
statements.agree: World power should be distributed among several independent major powers, without one dominant power.
statements.disagree: The world should not have several independent centres of power.
statements.note: This asks about the desired distribution of international power. It does not prescribe equal military strength, permanent hostility, regional conquest or a particular set of countries. Cooperation through international institutions is compatible with the statement unless those institutions replace independent centres of power.

statements.text: The value of goods is created by the labour that produces them.
statements.agree: What things are worth comes from the work put into them.
statements.disagree: The value of goods is not created by the labour that produces them.
statements.note: About whether the value of goods comes from the work that produces them. Workers deserving fair pay is a different question.

statements.text: Serving the nation means serving its working people.
statements.agree: The nation's cause and the cause of its ordinary working people are one and the same.
statements.disagree: Serving the nation does not mean serving its working people.
statements.note: About the nation's cause and its working people's cause being one and the same. Love of country alone is not enough.

statements.text: The political left should focus more on workers' material interests than on cultural identity issues.
statements.agree: The left should care more about workers' material interests than about cultural identity issues.
statements.disagree: The political left should give cultural identity issues at least as much attention as workers' material interests.
statements.note: About whether the left should give workers' pay, jobs and living costs more attention than cultural identity issues. Opposing identity causes is not required.

statements.text: A market economy is compatible with socialism under communist-party leadership.
statements.agree: A socialist system led by a communist party is able to include a market economy.
statements.disagree: A market economy is incompatible with socialism under communist-party leadership.
statements.note: About the compatibility of this economic model, not whether communist-party rule is desirable.

statements.text: Appointed public officials should be replaced after a limited time in office.
statements.agree: Appointed public officials should be replaced after a limited time in office.
statements.disagree: Appointed public officials need not be replaced after a limited time in office.
statements.note: About how long unelected officials, such as civil servants, should hold their posts. Term limits for elected officials are a different question.

statements.text: Money should be backed by precious metals.
statements.agree: Money should be backed by precious metals.
statements.disagree: Money does not need to be backed by precious metals.
statements.note: About whether a currency should be tied to precious metals, as under a gold standard, or be paper money not backed by metal.

statements.text: A government should pay off its national debt completely.
statements.agree: A government should pay off its national debt completely.
statements.disagree: A government need not pay off its national debt completely.
statements.note: About whether a country should carry a permanent national debt or try to eliminate it. Merely cutting the deficit is not enough.

statements.text: Indigenous peoples should be removed from their lands.
statements.agree: Indigenous peoples should be moved away from the lands they live on.
statements.disagree: Indigenous peoples should not be removed from their lands.
statements.note: About moving indigenous peoples off the lands they live on to territory elsewhere, often to open those lands to settlers.

statements.text: There should be no central bank.
statements.agree: There should be no central bank.
statements.disagree: There should be a central bank.
statements.note: About whether a country should have a central, national bank at all, whatever money it uses.

statements.text: In war, the enemy's civilians are legitimate targets.
statements.agree: In war, the enemy's civilians are legitimate targets.
statements.disagree: In war, the enemy's civilians are not legitimate targets.
statements.note: About whether civilians, not only fighters, may be chosen as targets in an armed conflict. Civilians killed as an unintended side effect of attacking fighters is a different question.

statements.text: Objects that people worship should be destroyed.
statements.agree: Objects that people worship should be destroyed.
statements.disagree: Objects that people worship should not be destroyed.
statements.note: About destroying objects and places of popular devotion, such as idols or shrines, as false worship. Opposing the worship without destroying anything is not enough.

statements.text: Starting a war to bring other peoples under a religion's rule is justified.
statements.agree: Starting a war to bring other peoples under a religion's rule is justified.
statements.disagree: War should never be started to bring other peoples under a religion's rule.
statements.note: About starting wars to bring other peoples under a religion's rule. Fighting only to defend the faith is a different question.

statements.text: Humanity has been declining since a past golden age.
statements.agree: Humanity has been declining since a past golden age.
statements.disagree: Humanity has not been declining since a past golden age.
statements.note: About whether humanity's overall condition has worsened since a past golden age, including decline within a recurring cycle of ages. Technical progress alone is not enough to deny it.

statements.text: A people should return to the religion it followed before a faith from another people replaced it.
statements.agree: A people whose old religion was displaced by one from outside should revive its original faith.
statements.disagree: A people need not return to the religion it followed before a faith from another people replaced it.
statements.note: About reviving a people's pre-conversion religion, such as European paganism, in place of a religion that came from elsewhere.

statements.text: A people's religion should grow out of that people's own character.
statements.agree: A people's religion should grow out of that people's own character.
statements.disagree: A people's religion need not grow out of that people's own character.
statements.note: About whether a people's religion should grow out of that people's own character. Simply practising a traditional religion is not enough.

statements.text: God has chosen one people to be superior to all other peoples.
statements.agree: God has chosen one people to be superior to all other peoples.
statements.disagree: God has not chosen any people to be superior to all other peoples.
statements.note: About divinely granted superiority of a people, not simply a people’s religious covenant or special duties.

statements.text: The state should support the ways of life it judges good.
statements.agree: Government should take sides on how people live, backing the ways of life it judges good.
statements.disagree: The state should stay neutral between its citizens' ways of life.
statements.note: About the state backing the ways of life it judges good, rather than staying neutral between them. Protecting people's freedom to choose is a different question.

statements.text: The state should promote the return of people of foreign ethnic origin to their ancestral countries, including those who hold citizenship.
statements.agree: The state should promote the return of people of foreign ethnic origin to their ancestral countries, including those who hold citizenship.
statements.disagree: The state should not promote the return of people of foreign ethnic origin to their ancestral countries, including those who hold citizenship.
statements.note: About a return policy based on ethnic origin, extending to citizens descended from immigrants. Promotion includes incentives; agreement does not by itself establish support for forced deportation.

statements.text: Keeping prices stable should be the first priority of economic policy.
statements.agree: Economic policy should put stable prices ahead of its other goals.
statements.disagree: Keeping prices stable should not be the first priority of economic policy.
statements.note: About whether keeping prices stable should come ahead of other economic goals such as full employment. Treating inflation as one goal among several is not enough.

statements.text: Immigration should be restricted on the basis of race.
statements.agree: Immigration should be restricted on the basis of race.
statements.disagree: Immigration should not be restricted on the basis of race.
statements.note: About choosing who may immigrate by race, whatever the total number admitted. Wanting fewer immigrants overall is a different question.

statements.text: Technology is never politically neutral.
statements.agree: Technology is never politically neutral.
statements.disagree: Technology is sometimes politically neutral.
statements.note: About whether technology carries political interests built into its design, not only in how people use it. Showing that some tools get misused is not enough.

statements.text: Labour should have priority over capital.
